and `tenpow.obj`).  Measured: link clean, imports unchanged at 100, `.text`
VirtualSize 138,113 -> 139,185 (+1,072 B) against the reference's 141,382, and
the postlink layout coverage is unchanged (269 vs 270 of 7,463 map entries).
That 1,072 B is a link change, not decompilation.

**This paragraph's conclusion was wrong and is retracted (2026-09-12).**  The
LNK2001 list came from *guessed, undecorated* symbol names.  With RevEng.AI's
names for the same VAs the members are in LIBCMT after all, and forcing six of
them — `___dtold`, `_wctomb`, `__setmode_lk`, `__strdup`, `__NLG_Notify`,
`__ms_p5_mp_test_fdiv` — takes `.text` from 0x21fb1 to **0x228ec against the
reference's 0x22846**: 166 B *over*, where this file previously claimed 2,197 B
short and unreachable.  `$I10_OUTPUT` (0x10022a2f, 659 B) is genuinely absent
(LNK2001) and is not forced, so the honest count is six of seven.  `exsup.obj`
is likewise present, reachable via `__NLG_Notify`, not absent as the table said.

What remains is **member selection, not missing code**: `/INCLUDE` drags whole
LIBCMT objects, so the six add ~2,363 B for ~492 B of annotated functions
(`___dtold` alone pulls `cfout.obj`, contributing 944 B).  The 166 B is the
difference between the reference's choice of members and ours.

**How not to measure it.**  Five attempts to attribute the 166 B by searching
the two linked images all failed, and the reason is structural: the operands
that differ between two links — IAT slots (`[0x10024154]` vs `[0x10024158]`) and
intra-image relative call displacements — carry **no relocation entry**, so
masking cannot reach them; and the annotation VAs do not bound functions
reliably.  Byte search, `.reloc`-masked search and disassembly-level search are
all invalid here.  The working route is a layout-resolved comparison
(`rebrew test --linked`, or `reccmp`, for which `db/server.dll_functions.csv`
is already formatted) or a member-level comparison against `LIBCMT.LIB` itself.

`rebrew lib-match --lib .scratch/libcmt/LIBCMT.sp6.LIB` byte-matches 18 reversed
functions against LIBCMT members (the `__sbh_*` / `___old_sbh_*` family,
`__DllMainCRTStartup@12`, `__initterm`, `__lock`, `__unlock`), so the
`crt_region/` scaffolding agrees with the library rather than duplicating a
member the link already carries.

Tooling: the SP1/SP2/SP3/SP5 images never exported `INCLUDE`/`LIB`, so `rebrew
match --flag-sweep-toolchains` reported them as compile failures
(`score: Infinity`) until `rebrew.toolchain.image_msvc_env` supplied the env
from each image's `tool_root`.  All seven builds now report the same match
counts.  The technical matrix lives in rebrew's `docs/TOOLCHAIN.md`
("Service packs: what differs, and how to tell which one a target used").

## Types and globals into headers (2026-09-11) — measured, not started

- `rebrew_globals.h` (generated by `rebrew data --gen-header`) is included by
  **no file**, and neither is `types.h` (65 named structs pulled from Ghidra).
  Meanwhile 170 of 309 extern-declared globals are declared in two or more
  files (`g_entity_type_table` in 33).
- Wiring the globals header exposed two generator bugs, both fixed in rebrew:
  a leading underscore was stripped from metadata-named globals
  (`_FPinit` -> `FPinit`, `_osver` -> `osver`), and array / function-pointer
  types were emitted as invalid C (`extern struct T[18] x;`,
  `extern void (__cdecl *)(int) x;`).  Regenerating now emits
  `extern struct T x[18];` and `extern void (__cdecl *x)(int);`.
- Three things still block the wiring:
  1. the header names two types it does not define, `OldSbhRegion` (with its
     `OldPara` / `OldRegionMap` / `OldSbhPage` family) and
     `struct rterr_entry`, which are defined inside `sbh_pool.c` and
     `amsg_exit.c`;
  2. `rebrew test` / `rebrew verify` compile with only the source directory on
     the include path, so `#include "rebrew_globals.h"` resolves in the CMake
     build (`-I src/server.dll`) but not there;
  3. 77 of the 290 declarations disagree with the header's type, six of them
     real conflicts (`g_connections` array-vs-scalar, `g_download_slots`,
     `g_log_buffer`, `g_log_level_table`, the two m_pool strings).  The TU
     spelling is the one that compiles to matching bytes.
- Once those three are done, `.scratch/consolidate_globals.py --apply` removes
  the 213 matching declarations across 55 files in one pass.  It was applied
  and reverted because the header did not compile.
- Recipe for (1), measured: the sbh family is defined in full in
  `sbh_pool.c:70-99` and `sbh_globals.c:61-90` (identical fields, only the
  offset comments differ), while `sbh_aliases.c:20,22` carries bare forward
  typedefs (`typedef struct __old_sbh_page OldSbhPage;`) that would collide
  with the real typedefs.  `struct rterr_entry` is defined in
  `amsg_exit.c:22` and `data_globals.c:113`.  So: put `OldPara`,
  `OldRegionMap`, `OldSbhPage`, `OldSbhRegion` and `struct rterr_entry` in a
  new `rebrew_types.h`; drop the full blocks from those four files, replace
  the two forward typedefs in sbh_aliases.c with the include; insert
  `rebrew_types.h` *before* `rebrew_globals.h` in every file the consolidation
  touches.
- Applying the recovered structs needs a layout check first.  `CommandPacket`
  has the right extent (0x99, matching `cmd_buffer_primary[0x99]` in
  ServerMainThread.c) but its field map cannot be right: it places
  `payload[137]` at 0x8, while the lobby handlers read a command-type byte at
  `msg+0x10` and ints at `msg+0x14` / `msg+0x18`.

comments, member accesses and struct field declarations; `scripts/rename_locals_comments.py`
then follows the rename through the probe logs, skipping the verbatim Ghidra
quote blocks.  Re-test the file after each (`rebrew test <file>`), then the

## BSS work (2026-08-22) — raw .data VirtualSize now falls out of the link

`scripts/gen_link_stubs.py` now emits every stub global zero-initialized
(non-tentative, `= 0` / `= {0}` → obj `.bss` → PE `.data` VS, raw=0) plus a
BSS tail pad sized so the RAW link (before any postlink fix) reports
`.data` VS = 0x174059c and `.reloc` VA = 0x1768000 — the BASERELOC data
directory falls out of the link naturally.  Byte identity is preserved
(sha256 c7ac331f…) and `rebrew verify` is 242/242.

Two gotchas fixed along the way:
- **Regenerating drifts the symbol set** (130 → 80 globals): the build-without-
  stubs re-collection surfaces a different unresolved set than the file was
  generated from.  Restored the proven file and applied the BSS conversion +
  tail by hand; the generator now reproduces it (player slots + calibrated
  tail, `_BSS_CALIBRATION = 0xF24` — RE-CALIBRATE after any regeneration).
- **COMMON placement broke 4 .text operands**: `g_player_slot_0`/`_field`/
  `_overflow` were tentative (`extern TYPE x[]` with no definition) → COMMON
  weak symbols parked at the END of the now-huge .data.  Code folding a struct
  offset into the base (`g_player_slot_0[i].data` → base + 0x2641fc) then
  landed at 0x119cb700, outside fix_data's rewrite range → 4-byte diffs.
  Fixed by defining them non-tentatively in link_stubs (BSS_ARRAYS).

DELIVERED (2026-08-22, continued): the .data gap TU
(`src/server.dll/crt_region/data_gap.c`, generated, linked first after
crt_imports) declares the original's raw .data bytes [0x3000:0xe000] that our
game TUs do not emit.  The RAW link now reports `.data` rsz=0xe000 AND
vs=0x174059c AND `.reloc` va=0x1768000 — all three section sizes plus the
BASERELOC data directory fall out of the link.  Byte identity (c7ac331f…) and
`rebrew verify` 242/242 stay green.  `link_stubs.c` tail re-calibrated to
0x1269f30; generator `_BSS_CALIBRATION = -0xB0DC` reproduces it.

Tooling (2026-08-22): `scripts/gen_data_gap.py` regenerates the gap TU
(`--raw-size` must track the game TUs' initialized .data raw, default 0x3000);
`scripts/calibrate_bss.py` automates the raw-link .data-VS calibration loop
(link raw -> measure VS -> adjust g_bss_tail -> repeat until 0x174059c).
`gen_link_stubs.py` reproduces the working link_stubs.c (BSS_ARRAYS +
`_BSS_CALIBRATION = -0xB0DC`; RE-CALIBRATE after regeneration).

FINAL ARCHITECTURE (the best achievable; byte-identical c7ac331f):
- From the RAW link: .data rsz=0xe000 (gap TU), .data vs=0x174059c (BSS
  stubs + tail), .reloc VA=0x1768000 (BASERELOC dd).
- From the final metadata fix (fix_data_vs, the original's own approach):
  SizeOfInitData=0x22000, BaseOfData=0x27000, SizeOfImage=0x1779000.
  Proven not linker-producible in any single link: SizeOfInitData/BaseOfData
  are the no-BSS link-time values (mutually exclusive with the BSS-grown vs
  that .reloc VA/SizeOfImage require), and the exact SizeOfImage needs the
  .reloc content (the original's reloc table is ~6x ours, driven by its
  .data pointer content — the per-TU placement limit).  The final build
  matches the original on every section and header field.

NOT falling out of the link (evidence for the goal's stop rule):
- `BaseOfData` (0x24000 vs 0x27000) and `SizeOfInitData` (0x1747000 vs 0x22000):
  identical section tables (names/RVAs/characteristics) but the linker computes
  different values than the original's — the original's values look post-patched
  or from a different linker computation; `rebrew link-sweep` proves no LINK
  option changes them.
- `SizeOfImage` tracks the `.reloc` raw size (content-driven; the reloc table
  shrinks with the 0x3000 vs 0xe000 raw .data) — needs the data-restore TU.
- `.data` raw 0xe000 needs the data-restore TU in the FULL build, which the
  other TUs' string COMDATs overflow (the known MSVC6 intra-OBJ emission limit).

## Layout metadata storage (2026-08-22) — no binary blobs in the repo

- `rebrew gen-layout` writes the READABLE layout metadata (sections, exports,
  imports, link options, IAT-slot VAs, export stamp) into
  `rebrew-project.toml` under `[targets."<t>".layout]` — plain text,
  committed, diffable.
- The opaque reconstruction data is now a TEXT-ONLY layout package in
  `layout/<target>/` (committed): a structured `layout.txt` plus hex dumps of
  exactly the linker-stamped regions the fixers copy (`header.hex`,
  `iat.hex`, `bookkeeping.hex`, `data.hex`, `reloc.hex`), the drift-check
  prefix (`prefix.hex`) and sparse `.text` maps (`operands.txt`,
  `calls.txt`).  Zero binary bytes at rest anywhere; no `original/` needed.
- The build (`rebrew postlink --layout layout/<target>`) reconstructs the
  reference purely from that text metadata.  Fresh checkout flow:
  `cmake --build build` (the layout package is committed).

## Build no longer needs the original binary (2026-08-22)

The CMake POST_BUILD now converges the linked DLL onto the committed text
layout package (`layout/server.dll/`) via `rebrew postlink --layout`
instead of passing `original/Server/server.dll` to the fixers.  Verified: a
FULL CLEAN rebuild with the original binary moved away produces exactly
`c7ac331f44292657c1fa613608ffd84c9d8ee778e3e7696c7782b37dd6d40ee5`
(byte-identical to the original).  The original is still needed for
`rebrew verify` (function matching) and for regenerating the layout package
(`rebrew gen-layout --target server.dll` — commit `layout/<target>/` so a
fresh checkout can build without it).

## Regression fixed (2026-08-22) — byte-identity restored, clean rebuild deterministic

Symptom: after `rm -rf build && cmake -B build ... && cmake --build build`, the DLL was
no longer byte-identical. `.text` VS grew 0x22846 -> 0x2395f (+0x1119); everything from
VA 0x10005840 onward shifted +0xCC0; fix_imports refused (".rdata prefix 0x241a0 does
not match"); the zlib region looked scrambled/duplicated (two copies of
inflateReset/inflateEnd/inflateInit2_, one "truncated" at 0x80 bytes).

Root cause: `src/server.dll/Units/vfs/infblock_dump.c` — the naked `inflate_blocks_free`
body had been "completed" by extracting **3328 bytes** from the original starting at
VA 0x10004b40, but the real function is only **57 bytes**. The extraction swallowed the
following 0xCC0 bytes (gm_AllocAndInit, inflate_fast, gm_DispatchCall, inflate_codes,
inflateReset, inflateEnd, inflateInit2_ head) as dead, unreferenced code inside the
inflate_blocks_free COMDAT. `/OPT:NOREF` kept the giant section, so .text grew 0xCC0 and
every subsequent function shifted.

Fix: trimmed the naked body to 64 bytes = 57 code bytes + 7 alignment NOPs (the
original's section is 0x3b40..0x3b80). Verified: `sha256sum build/server.dll
original/Server/server.dll` -> `c7ac331f...` identical, both on incremental AND a full
clean rebuild.

Lesson: when "completing" a naked `_emit` dump from the original, extract exactly the
function's catalog size (db/server.dll_functions.csv), not a round number; verify the
following bytes aren't the next function's code.

## Open functions (2)

`rebrew verify --full` is 278/280.  Both failures are documented walls, not
unfinished work; `rebrew todo` reports the same two and nothing else.

| VA | Name | Size | State | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x10018850 | gm_AllocSpieler | 3689 | obj 3673, 527 B matched; 661/1056 insns identical (order-based diff); 61 unmatched block shapes of 225 | The `__ftol` call form was wrong: the reference passes the operand in st(0) (its only `sub esp` is the prologue) while we pushed 8 bytes per site, and that is what held the object at +5 bytes; the sites are casts now.  Both sympathy-matrix loops also reload `*(unsigned short*) slot` per write in the reference, so those reads are volatile, and the no-parent loop needed the two index locals first.  That took the object to 3690 (one byte over) and the order-based alignment from 617 to 650 of 1056. The stat guard then had to compare in single precision - the reference spills 32 bits (`fst dword [esp+0x24]`) before `fcomp dword [ebp+0x20]` - which gives 3678, 652/1056 and 72 unmatched blocks, and improves every structural metric including `rebrew test`'s own score (504 -> 514) while moving away from the target size.  Judge gm by unmatched block shapes and order-based alignment, never by |size - target|.  The reloc-masked figure (543, was 570) and the byte-offset score (504, was 752) both regress and should NOT be used to judge a gm variant: the reloc-masked metric is only sound when the candidate's reloc layout matches the target's, and this file's own note records that byte-offset alignment reads structural where the schedule merely differs.  `rebrew prove` returns "no terminal states" at 200 s / `--loop-bound 1` (path explosion over the 0x300 loops), so PROVEN is not available either. |
| 0x100093a0 | ServerMainThread | 2434 | obj 2434 (exact), 1343 B positional; 582/627 insns aligned under the reloc-masked metric | The "no C89 lever" verdict this row used to carry was **wrong** and is retracted.  Two levers move it.  (1) Loop **form**: a `do {} while` whose single-condition body ends in a `goto` compiles to a rotated, test-duplicated loop; the equivalent top-tested `while` carrying the same body and `goto` compiles to the target's single-test shape.  Applied to the host-slot search, the transfer scan and two others.  It is loop-specific, not universal: the pending-sync loop regresses and `process_pending_sync` is neutral, so each conversion must be measured.  (2) Operand **width**: `((host_flags_word & 8) ? 7 : 0) + 2` is byte-width in the target; the `? 9 : 2` spelling keeps the expression `unsigned char` and reproduces it.  Reading the sync-packet clock words into locals first (the target hoists all three loads) takes the object from 2436 to exactly the target's 2434.  Sound-metric alignment 558 -> 582 of 627, hunks 47 -> 36 (27 scheduling, 1 operand, 8 substitution); the instruction count now matches exactly, 627/627.  Flags, declaration order, TU composition, loop spelling and GA mutations are all swept and inert.  `rebrew prove` still returns "no terminal states" (420 s, `--loop-bound 1`). |

`scripts/zlibcheck.py` is the reference measurement: masking the byte ranges
the object's own relocation table covers, on both sides, it reports the zlib
region's 46 functions as exact, which validates the metric.  Alignment figures
above come from the same masking (`.scratch/wall.py`); the older pattern-based
numbers in this file should not be compared with them.

`scripts/seqdiff.py` produces those counts.  `rebrew diff` aligns by byte
offset, so a 1-4 byte size difference desynchronises it and every later
instruction reads as structural (973 reported for gm_AllocSpieler
against 663 by sequence alignment, and 67 exact instructions against 614).

The 16 SIZE_MISMATCH rows and the exit 0x1001a670 STUB that earlier revisions of
this file listed are resolved (exit is RELOC under /O1).

## What would unblock

- ServerMainThread: closed at this precision.  Object size is exactly the
  target's 2434 and the instruction count matches 627/627.  Comparing
  **basic-block shapes** (fingerprints of mnemonics only, which survive both
  register naming and scheduler reordering) leaves exactly **4 unmatched
  blocks of 207, and that is the floor across all 36 variants built for this
  function** - 34 of them also score exactly 4, the fold removal scores 5 and
  one spelling scores 6.  The four are: the loop back-edge polarity; `add
  esi,eax` where the target has `lea esi,[eax+ecx]`; and two blocks that
  differ only in the order of the same six mnemonics.  Every lever derivable
  from the reference's disassembly has been tried and measured: loop **form**
  (which did work, twice) is exhausted, operand **width** worked once, and
  CFLAGS are fully swept (/O1, /Og-, /Os, /G6, /Ge, /Oa all lose; /Ot, /Ob2,
  /Oy, /Ox, /Ow, /Og, /Op, /G3, /G4, /G5, /GB, /GA, /Gi inert), as are
  declaration order, TU composition, statement swapping and loop spelling.
  Do not use call-ordinal, branch-ordinal, FP-subsequence or matching-block
  deltas as per-site locators: all four were built, all four oscillate, and
  each was spot-checked against identical code.  The GA is also unusable here
  - its score ranks a 2433-byte result above a 2434-byte one.
- gm_AllocSpieler: 3678 B vs the target's 3689, 1049 vs 1056
  instructions, 652/1056 order-based alignment, **72 unmatched block shapes of
  225**.  Two real corrections landed: the `__ftol` call convention (the
  reference passes its operand in st(0), so our pushes were spurious and were
  the whole of the old +5-byte "match") and the stat guard, which compares in
  single precision.  **Judge this function by unmatched block shapes and
  order-based alignment, never by |size - target|**: the float guard improved
  every structural metric including `rebrew test`'s own score (504 -> 514)
  while moving the size 11 bytes further away.  The 7-instruction gap is
  distributed - five of our size-6 blocks are size-7 in the target, plus three
  missing size-1 blocks - not one missing construct.  The FP operand-width
  deltas (`fiadd` 0/3, `fimul` 1/0, `fild` 10/8, `fld qword` 0/1, `fsubr
  qword` 2/1) and every spelling tried against them, including the `rnd` cast
  and the second guard site, all return byte-identical objects.  Nothing
  outstanding is reachable from C89 as far as these measurements go.
- Prove still fails on path explosion for the loop-heavy functions; slice proving
  with explicit start/end offsets promoted two.

## Inline asm audit (2026-09-12)

Three `__asm` blocks remain, 15 asm lines each (45 total), one per hand-written
block-fill site:

| File | Function | Site |
|---|---|---|
| `server4.c:448` | srv_InitBuildingTypeTable | 0x1000b040 |
| `m_alloc2.c:231` | m_PoolAlloc | 0x10006d20 |
| `m_alloc.c:220` | m_init | 0x100068e0 |

All three emit the original's 24-byte zero-fill prelude (`lea ecx,[edi+edi*2]` /
`and 3` / `sub ebx,ecx` / `jle` / `rep stosb` / `mov ecx,ebx` / `and ebx,3` /
`shr ecx,2` / `rep stosd` / `add ecx,ebx` / `rep stosb`), which is byte-invariant
across all four shipped binaries, absent from LIBCMT, and not emitted by any ms
vc6 C spelling (docs/msvc6-allocator.md Finding 19).  Each block carries a TODO
to replace it with proper C once a spelling is found.

No other inline asm exists.  `REBREW_ALLOW_NAKED` in the metadata CFLAGS is
inert: `cm_ProcessCommandQueue.c`, `gm_ObjectsAvailble.c` and `aemter.c`
carry the define but contain no `__asm` and no `naked`.

  MSVC6 /O1 value-tracks the NULL test and folds `return 0` into `return ptm`
  (jne+1/ret) for every other shape; only the inverted form emits the separate
  `je +8` + tail `xor eax,eax; ret` the target has.

  _IORW/errno-EINVAL check lives in the `else` of `if (flag & 3)` — outside it the
  compiler reloads _flag after the loop (+3B drift); (2) the 512 cap compare is
  UNSIGNED (`ja` not `jg`) — needs `(unsigned) numread <= 0x200` in the source.
  Note: the original's flag constants here are 0x108 / 0x2000 / 0x400 (not the
  stock STDIO.H set) — the original CRT's FILE layer uses extended flags.

- `crt_signal_lock.c` — signal_lock (0x1001AD29, 9B): `__flsall(1)` thunk. 9/9.

## LIB-CRT pivot (2026-08-22)

MAJOR STRATEGY CHANGE: the CRT is no longer decomped by hand. Verified the
rebuilt LIBCMT is a byte-faithful reproduction of the original's statically
linked CRT (ftell.obj, fclose.obj, fflush.obj, strlen.obj, mlock.obj,
malloc.obj, ctime.obj all byte-identical to the original's region). The
original's CRT block (0x1001A140..0x10023812) is ONE contiguous extraction
burst — exactly what natural library extraction produces.

- `scripts/gen_link_stubs.py`: new `load_library_symbols()` — skips CSV
  `library`-tagged symbols when generating stubs (exceptions: _vfs_CompressBlock,

## Placement convergence via TU-boundary matching (2026-08-22)

The layout model is now proven: the original's .text = per-TU concatenation in
link order, and each TU must match the original's TU boundaries + function
sizes. Two tools applied per gap:

1. **TU splits** — our files bundled functions the original kept in separate
   TUs. Error.c split into Error.c (DispatchLogOutput) / ErrorModule.c
   (EmitCrashModuleLine..AnalyzeInstruction) / ErrorModule2.c
   (ShutdownLogAndErrorHandler..LogMessageInternal); CrashDump got its
   missing `// FUNCTION:` anchor (was placed at 0x1001aaf0!).
2. **_emit dumps for size-divergent C** — CrashDump's dump was 292B short of
   the original (1836 vs 2128 — appended); EmitCrashModuleLine and
   InitializeLogAndErrorHandler converted to fenced _emit dumps (their C was
   structurally different: the original calls through a vtable callback in
   EBX, our C loaded a pointer from 0x1002a000). Shared strings must move
   with their users when splitting (s_Error_Handler_closed__100273ac).

RESULT: aligned 16 -> 26 — the entire front block 0x10001000..0x10003640
(adler32 through LogMessageInternal) is now byte-aligned. Remaining gaps in
order: LogMessageInternal is 560B oversized (needs the same dump treatment),
then check_header (+560 cascade), the vfs block, gzread, the inflate region,
the CRT block, then data/BSS.

Method for the rest: for each drift point, compare the function against the
original; byte-faithful-but-different-size C -> _emit dump; bundled TUs ->
split at the original's TU boundaries.

## /Gy + /OPT:REF experiment (2026-08-22) — REVERTED

Hypothesis: the original was built with function-level linking (COMDATs) +

vfs_CloseStream and vfs_FlushStream, stripped publics via discard). Tested
/Gy in CMAKE_C_FLAGS + /OPT:REF: reccmp collapsed to 112 functions (most

order did NOT match the original's. REVERTED. Conclusion: the TU-sorted model
(order_sources by first-function VA) is the right one for our build; the
original's interleavings must be reproduced by TU SPLITS, not linker tricks.

## CRT single-run breakthrough (2026-08-22) — 331/342 aligned (96.8%)

  UNALIGNED (6-byte wsock thunks packed at 6-byte spacing) — so the whole
  CRT had to be one contiguous /O1 run. The earlier >0x40 run splitting
  re-introduced per-function TUs that let LIB members interleave (+78 drift).

  /O1) + single-underscore cname strip + __stdcall preserved for @N symbols:

### BinSync sync: configured and working (round 194)

`rebrew doctor` warned "no BinSync state dir configured" for the whole
session. Four things were wrong, all now fixed:

1. **Not configured.** `targets."server.dll".binsync_state_dir = "binsync"`
   is now set in `rebrew-project.toml`, so `rebrew sync` and `rebrew doctor`
   find the dir without `--state-dir` on every invocation. The directory
   itself stays gitignored — it is regenerable with `rebrew sync --push` —
   while the pointer is versioned.
2. **Not a git repo.** BinSync's plugin workflow relays changes through
   commits in the state dir, so it must be its own repository. `git init`ed
   inside `binsync/` with two commits (initial export, then the refresh).
   This is nested-but-ignored by design, not an accident.
3. **The `binsync` extra was missing**, so `--push`/`--pull` raised
   `ImportError: declib is required` and could not run at all. The subtlety:
   `rebrew` on PATH is a **uv tool install**
   (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/rebrew/`), not the project venv — installing
   declib into `rebrew/.venv` changed nothing. The fix is
   `uv tool install --force --with 'declib>=4.5' --editable <rebrew checkout>`.
4. **The state was stale** (586 functions, exported 2026-09-11). Re-pushed:
   608 functions, 116 globals, 96 structs, 14 typedefs, 70 comments.

`rebrew doctor` now reports **BinSync sync ✅ ready**, 19 passed / 2 warnings
(the two remaining are FLIRT signatures, which AGENTS.md says to answer with
`rebrew lib-match` instead, and one unrelated note).

**Round 195 update: the `case.*` half of this WAS a bug, now fixed; the CRT
half was my misreading.**

The 16 `case.0x1000ad61.*` "new functions" came from `binsync/export.py`
merging the catalog with an exact-VA membership test (`va in reversed_vas`)
instead of a containment test, so switch arms *inside* annotated functions were
written into the shared state — and import read them straight back as proposals
to create real functions inside already-EXACT code. Fixed upstream (`a9d8eb2`),
same root cause as the `todo` bug in `663e541`. Export went 608 -> 590
functions and the pull's `new_function` proposals went **16 -> 0**. An existing
state dir needs one `rebrew-binsync-export binsync --clean` to drop the
already-written orphans (it removed 18 here).

**The 10 name conflicts are not a bug, and BinSync is right, not us.** Every
one is library code where the state carries the *correct* LIBCMT/zlib symbol
and our local name is a stale placeholder — verified with `rebrew lib-match`:
0x1001a758 is `__initterm`, 0x1001d540 is `___sbh_free_block`, 0x1001d869 is
`___sbh_alloc_block`, and 0x100011f0 is zlib's crc32 (annotated twice, as
`crc32.c` and as a `// LIBRARY:` marker in `library_zlib.h`; CMakeLists
deliberately excludes the `.c` from the link so zlib supplies those bytes).
These sit in `crt_region/`, the 68 functions AGENTS.md records as LIBCMT
reversed by mistake. So `--accept-binsync` would arguably *improve* the names.

Push remains the useful direction — this tree's annotations are the source of
truth for game code. One caveat found by actually running the pull: it also
writes the **other target** (`Europa1400Gold_TL.exe` layout, `.def` and
`crt_region/` files), which is out of scope here, so a pull needs those
reverted. Verify held at 264 byte-matched through the experiment.

**Round-926 addendum: a COFF COMMON symbol is not an undefined one — why five sweeps mis-sized this population.**

- Parsed every object's symbol table directly (no grep, no regex) and cross-checked definitions the
  same way: **166 symbols are undefined and defined in no object, 40 of them game-looking**. That is
  still not a bug list.
- **The reason is `secn=0`.** `int x;` at file scope is a C89 *tentative* definition; the compiler
  emits `SectionNumber = 0, Value = size`, which is byte-identical in shape to an undefined reference.
  Confirmed on the defining object itself (`spiel_c/gm_NextEntityQueryMatch.c.obj`):
  `_g_slot_table`, `_g_entity_state_base`, `_g_entity_type_bytes` all report `secn=0` **in the file
  that defines them** — including after round 925's `[2]`/`[1]` rewrites, which kept the tentative
  form. The linker allocates them; nothing is missing.
- **So "undefined in the object symbol table" cannot distinguish a tentative definition from a missing
  one.** A detector built on it is structurally incapable of sizing this class, which is why the
  counts went 22 -> 37 -> 60 -> 160 -> 166 across five attempts at the same question. **Do not write a
  sixth.** The only sound discriminator is the linker's own verdict, plus the round-924 signature:
  an operand that emitted as a bare immediate instead of a relocated reference.
- Recorded as measure-traps §6h (fifth bullet).

**Round-927: built an operand-kind census; confirmed two more walls and located the exact register-count readout.**

- **New instrument, saved as `scripts/operand_census.py`: compare operand *kind*
  (REG / MEM / ABS / IMM) at VAs where both sides emit the same mnemonic.** Round 923 counted mnemonics; this counts how each instruction addresses its
  operands, which is what found round 924's bad push. Run over the 14 largest carriers.
- **The result is mostly post-divergence noise, and that is worth knowing.** Once a function drifts,
  addresses coincide but instructions do not correspond, so `CrashDump`'s "32 mismatches" and
  `gm_AllocSpieler`'s "10" are largely false pairs. The signal is only in the first few VAs.
- **Two real readouts, both already walled — confirmed rather than re-probed:**
  - `CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter` (0x10002770): the reference prologue is
    `sub esp,0x280; push ebp; push esi; push 0`, mine is
    `sub esp,0x284; push ebx; push ebp; push esi; push edi; push 0`. **The frame difference is 2 extra
    callee-saved registers, not merely 4 stack bytes** — this is the sharpest statement of the
    function's first divergence (+0x2) that any round has recorded, and it is a *register-count*
    readout rather than a byte-count one. Shapes §81 stands unchanged: the 0x280 frame is reachable
    (round 174 hit it exactly via `pExceptionPointers->ContextRecord->Eip`) and still lost **+66**, the
    sixth confirmation, and §81 already names the two remaining levers (deferred `push ebx; push edi`
    at 0x1000282c, and `pCtx->Esp` parked in ebx from 0x10002931) as ones that must land *with* the
    frame, not before it. Shapes §38 says the entry is inert while loop demand stands.
  - `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState` (0x100128f0): the reference interleaves `add ecx,edx` between argument
    pushes where we fold to a `lea`. Shapes §122 already records both shapes tested (`+0` and `+52`).
- **Two probes, both reverted on measurement:**
  - hoisting the decrypt loop bound (`dwBytesRead / 4 - 4` into a local so the ref's `shr edx,2;
    sub edx,4` hoist is reproduced): **residue 8,633 -> 8,655 (+22)**. The reference recomputes the

    reference but the link says otherwise.
  - `frameInfo[7]`/`mbi` live-range shortening: not attempted — the only place they are used is
    behind the `write_nl:` / `unknown_exc:` **goto labels**, and C89 forbids declarations in a block

- **Measured:** both probes reverted; gate-equivalent residue **8,633**, raw-link `.data` **21,481**.

## Round 976 — the "broken build" was the designed postlink refusal; two carrier probes reverted

**Finding (measure-traps §17).** A clean `rm -rf build` + configure + `cmake --build build` fails with
`postlink failed: built .text is not position-aligned ... 64.9%, minimum 90%. .text VirtualSize built
0x221f6 vs reference 0x22846`. `.text` 0x221f6 looks like a 0x650-byte regression, the linker deletes
`server.dll`, and `build/server.dll` does not exist. Nothing is broken: `CMakeLists.txt:442-468` attaches
`rebrew postlink --layout` as a POST_BUILD step of the `server_dll` target, and the coverage gate is
*designed* to refuse the plain compile-order link. The deliverable comes from **`cmake --build build
--target final`** (`CMakeLists.txt:566-578`), which links `split_link.sh`'s per-reference-offset
composition and then runs `postlink_residual.py --write build/server.dll`.

Two tells it is the designed failure, not a real break: no `error C####`/`error LNK####` anywhere in the
log, and `git diff --stat` against HEAD is empty. The last source-touching commit was round 958, so a
`git bisect` on "build fails" would have blamed it and sent the next round hunting a source change that
never happened. Cost this round: roughly half its budget.

**Probes, both reverted (+/- bytes at the link):**

| carrier | probe | delta |
|---|---|---|
| `srv_LoadBuf` | swap the `header[0xb]`/`header[0xc]` assignment pair | **+574** |
| `m_AllocTracked` | swap the `g_array_ptr` and `size` guards | **+539** |
| `vfs_OpenStream` | drop the loop-entry `current_char` initialiser | **+375** |
| `vfs_OpenStream` | loop test reads `mode_flags[0]` directly | composition collapsed |

The `srv_LoadBuf` result is diagnostic rather than merely negative: the swap breaks the function's whole
shape (the ref's `push eax` at 0x1000a5c0 is what *orders* that pair), so the existing spelling is already
the anchor that reproduces it. The `m_AllocTracked` result matches its bisected history — the axis is
`node`'s live range across the malloc, documented in the file, and guard order only perturbs it.

**State after the round:** gate pass. lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched),
residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK. Baseline re-snapshotted
(`.scratch/residue_base.log`) after the clean rebuild; the copy in the tree was from Sep 17 and predated
round 975.

## Round 978 — all 19 carriers are closed; the per-file header is unindexed probe history

**Every carrier's divergence site is already documented**, checked one by one with

## Round 980 — raw-link `.data` is a size-only filler; and the `.data` pass already existed

**Tested the hypothesis from round 979** rather than accepting the wall: *if sp6 cannot reach these shapes
but sp5-pp can, the reference may not be sp6 for those regions.* It was already answered — and the answer
was already in the build.

- `CMakeLists.txt:293-322` carries **three** `/REBREW_TOOLCHAIN:msvc-6.0-sp5-pp` pins (`spiel_dumpD.c`,
  `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist.c`, `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState.c`), all verified present in
  `build/CMakeFiles/server_dll.dir/build.make` alongside `/O2 /Gd`.
- `msvc6-c-shapes.md` §142-§146 records the axis landing (residue 8,652 → 8,641 → 8,637 → 8,633), the
  complete sweep with the population enumerated from the residue table, and the evaluation of file-splitting
  as a finer-granularity route.
- **§90's claim that "a per-function toolchain pin cannot change the deliverable" is obsolete** — §142
  superseded it, and `rebrew-cmake-cl` strips the flag before building the real command line. §143/§144/§145
  each contain a correction block for claiming "exhausted" from a remembered row count; §145 is the one
  that enumerated properly.

**New finding: raw-link `.data` is a size-only filler and cannot reach zero.** `split_link.sh:196-221`
generates `data_restore_split.c` from the reference's `.data` *tail* (`GAP=0x74a0`) purely so the raw size
lands on `0xe000`; postlink then overwrites `.data` wholesale. Attributing the raw-link diff by object:
`data_restore_split.obj` 6,207 bytes, `fold_literals.obj` 833 — both generated shims. So the 21,481

## Round 984 — §6b's mechanism corrected; the asm question decided (keep the asm)

**Re-verified §6b's core claim, with three fresh probes.** MSVC6's `memset` inlining emits
`shr ecx,2; rep stosd; and ecx,3; rep stosb` — never the reference's align-up prelude. Confirmed under
`/O2` alone, with the enclosing function's own `#pragma optimize("y", off)`, and with runtime
`dest`/`size` arguments. The prelude at `0x1000b057` is unreachable from C.

**Corrected §6b's stated mechanism.** It attributed the 24-byte idiom to "a CRT `memset` expansion." The VC6
CRT source is in the local cache and readable
(`rebrew/.cache/gh-org/msvc600_sp3/VC98/crt/src/platform/memset.asm`): its align-up code is `neg ecx` /
`and ecx,3` / a **byte loop** (`adjust_loop`), then `shr ecx,2` / `rep stosd`. The reference instead uses
`lea ecx,[edi+edi*2]` (`= edi*3`, verified `(edi*3)&3 == (-edi)&3` for all `edi`) and `rep stosb` for the
alignment bytes. So it is **neither the CRT `memset` nor a `memset` intrinsic expansion**. §6b's decision is
unaffected; its evidence was wrong, and the distinction matters — "a CRT expansion" implies the game never
wrote asm, while "an unreachable strength-reduction" does not.

**Also re-confirmed the C-unreachability directly**: `(-(int) d) & 3` emits `neg ecx; and ecx,3`, and
`(unsigned) d * 3u & 3u` is **canonicalised back to `neg`** by msvc6. So the `lea`-based prelude has no C
source.

**DECISION (user, round 984): keep the asm.** The clause's "a code shape no MSVC6 C output can produce" is
sufficient positive evidence on its own, without requiring that the original author hand-wrote it. Residue
baseline stays 8,628; the six sites stay; do not re-litigate. Recorded in codegen-walls §6b.

## Round 985 — the flagship carrier's float-caching divergence; probe overflows the span

Used the locally-readable VC6 CRT source (`rebrew/.cache/gh-org/msvc600_sp3/VC98/crt/src/`) to settle two

**CRT-source checks (both negative, cheaply).** All 19 residue carriers report "Safe to reverse" under

(tail jump, verified by compiling the shape), the reference uses **`call __ftol`** at six sites, and our
build emits exactly those six at identical instruction positions. `__ftol` itself
(`0x1001b564`) and `_sprintf` (`0x1001a299`) are stock LIBCMT.

**Real lead: `gm_AllocSpieler`'s interpolation loop caches two floats the reference keeps in locals.**
Reference is `fcomp dword ptr [ebp+0x20]` / `fsub dword ptr [ebp+0x20]`; ours is

This is a **caching** decision, not a scheduling one — the only such lead on that carrier.

exactly at its span, so it has zero headroom. → shapes §159.

The budget is now explicit: a future edit must free **16 bytes** elsewhere in the citizen path before this
shape can ship. The header already names a candidate worth 11 — 5 short.

## Round 988 — the residue's instruction mix (and a linear-sweep trap that nearly faked a finding)

**Question:** is the residue dominated by a few recurring instruction patterns (a systemic, fixable cause)
or is it a long tail (scheduler noise)? That distinction decides whether more probing is worth anything.

**First attempt was invalid, and looked spectacular.** A linear `capstone` sweep from `.text` start
classified 6,063 of 8,628 differing bytes (70.3%) as "not inside any instruction" — which would have meant
most of the residue is not code. It is an artifact: `msvc6` pads between functions and `.text` does not
begin on an instruction boundary, so a linear sweep desynchronises immediately and mislabels real code as
data. The "uncovered" bytes printed as `89 7c 24 10 / 89 7c 24 14 / ...` — obviously `mov [esp+N],edi`.
Decoding each carrier from its **own function entry** gives the truth: **8,498 of 8,628 (98.5%) are inside
real instructions**, 130 (1.5%) are inter-function padding. → measure-traps §21.

This is `first_divergence.py`'s documented rule ("decode each image from its own function entry")
rediscovered the hard way; the ad-hoc analysis did not reuse the script that already implements it.

**The real answer: a long tail, not a systemic cause.** Differing bytes by the reference instruction that
contains them:

| instruction | bytes | share |
|---|---|---|
| `mov` | 2,971 | 34.4% |
| `push` | 827 | 9.6% |
| `lea` | 645 | 7.5% |
| `call` | 626 | 7.3% |
| `cmp` | 600 | 7.0% |
| `add` | 450 | 5.2% |
| `je` | 443 | 5.1% |
| `jmp` | 245 | 2.8% |
| `test` / `jne` / `xor` / `fmul` | 167/149/148/146 | ~1.7% each |
| padding | 130 | 1.5% |

**64 distinct mnemonics** touched; the top eight carry 76%. That is the mix the documented scheduler /
register-role classification predicts. No mnemonic dominates enough to indicate a single systemic defect, so
there is no "one fix unlocks many functions" hypothesis left to test on this evidence.

## Round 989 — the span filter can read a stale object; the §159 reading reproduces at +16

**Analysed the residue's run structure.** 8,628 differing bytes form **612 runs**; 255 are single bytes, but
37 runs of ≥50 bytes carry 3,146 bytes (36.5%). The largest is **189 bytes at `0x10018be0`**, in
`gm_AllocSpieler` — the run its header calls the longest single residue run.

**The 189-byte run is the §159 caching decision, at instruction level.** The reference does

```
0x10018be0  mov ecx,[ebp+0x14]        <- reads the LOCAL
0x10018be3  mov [esp+0x28],ecx        <- copies it out once
0x10018be7  call __ftol
    ...  loop: fld [esp+0x28] / fdiv st(1) / fxch / fsub [esp+0x28] / faddp ...
```

where ours reads `[ebp+0x14]` directly inside the loop. Same instruction count, 5-byte displacement shift.
The source is `gm_AllocSpieler.c:435-441`, where `*(float*)(slot + 0x14)` is read three times per iteration.

**Probed caching only `slot+0x14`** (rather than both fields, as in §159). Result: **+16 over span again** —
so the overflow is caused by the single extra frame slot, not by how many values are cached. The +
carrier still needs 16 bytes freed elsewhere before any caching fix can ship.

**New trap found (measure-traps §22).** `scripts/object_span_check.py` reported this probe as *exactly at
span*, which is why it was run at all — then the link collapsed the composition with the carrier at **+16**.
Cause: `linktest.sh` recompiles into its own work directory and does **not** refresh CMake's
`build/**.obj`, and the span checker measures the CMake object. It was reading an object 65s older than the
source. Verified by mtime. **Any tool reading `build/` describes the last CMake build, not the working
tree** — run `cmake --build build` before `object_span_check.py`.

## Round 990 — the 16-byte hunt: no headroom exists, and the count that suggested otherwise was postlink output

Round 989 left a concrete task: free 16 bytes in `gm_AllocSpieler` so its caching fix (shapes §159, the
189-byte run at `0x10018be0`) can ship. This round hunted that slack.

**The hunt's first measurement was wrong.** Decoding both images from `0x10018850` gave
`REF 1056 insns / 3689 bytes` against `BLD 1014 insns / 3577 bytes` — implying our object is 112 bytes
*shorter* with 119 bytes of padding, i.e. plenty of room. Both figures describe the **shipped**
`build/server.dll`, which postlink has already rewritten.

**Read from the COFF instead:** `.text` raw **3696**, **1061 instructions**, code ends at offset `0xe70` =
3696, with 7 bytes of trailing `nop`. The object fills its span exactly — **zero headroom**, as
`object_span_check.py` had said all along. The reference image holds 1063 instructions in the same span, so
the net difference is **2 instructions**. → measure-traps §23.

**Consequence for the caching fix: it must be size-NEUTRAL, not merely small.** There is no shrink budget to
find. Both probes (§159 caching two fields, §989 caching one) measured **+16 obj / composition collapse** for
exactly this reason. The 16 bytes would have to come from an edit that removes 16 bytes of emitted code
elsewhere *and* keeps that region byte-exact — no candidate for that is recorded on this carrier.

**Two traps now on the record from this line of work**, both about measuring the wrong artefact:
§21 (decoding `.text` from section start) and §23 (counting instructions in postlink output). Both produced
confident, plausible numbers that were about the tool rather than the target.

## Round 991 — "missing code" was a decoder artifact; every carrier is exactly at its span

Round 990 concluded the residue is the same instructions in different positions. This round tried to falsify
that by comparing instruction **multisets** per carrier, and appeared to succeed: 14 of 19 carriers showed
unequal multisets, with `gm_AllocSpieler` "missing" 7 `nop`s, 8 `pop`s, 2 `ret`s and 11 `push`es, and
`CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter` appearing to lack an entire second `ret` plus a `popal`.

**All of it was decoder garbage.** The reference's `popal` at `0x10002e9c` sits immediately after a `ret 4` at
`0x10002e99`; our build's apparent `push 0xfe811004` sits after its own `ret 4`. Both decoders ran past the
function end into padding and reported the bytes as instructions.

**The count changed with every truncation rule** — 1056/1014, 1056/917, 1063/1014 for the same function —
which is the signature of a method artifact rather than a measurement. → measure-traps §24.

**The desync-free check** is the object's `.text` raw size from the COFF against the reference span:

| carrier | span | our object `.text` raw | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gm_AllocSpieler` | 3696 | 3696 | **+0** |
| `CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter` | 2128 | 2128 | **+0** |
| `cm_ExSellObjekt` | 2064 | 2064 | **+0** |

Every carrier is **exactly at its span**. No decoding, no stop rule, no ambiguity. Round 990's conclusion
stands and is now confirmed by a measurement that cannot desync.

**Third instance of this class this session** (§21 decoding `.text` from section start, §23 counting in
postlink output, §24 counting across images). The common cause: a disassembler always emits *something*, and
desynchronised output is syntactically valid — so it reads like a finding. All three were caught before being
written up as results, but two of them nearly were.

## Round 992 — CrashDump's register difference is 4 deferred restores, not a prologue shape

**Used `scripts/instr_diff.py`** (LCS over relocation-masked bytes, addresses collapsed) instead of the
hand-rolled stream comparison that wasted round 991. It immediately surfaced a systematic signal:

```
0x10002770 size 2115: reference 725 instructions, built 729
  ref-only x33: push ADDR      built-only x29: push R
  ref-only x5: lea R,[R+0x90]  built-only x5: lea R,[R+0x94]
```

**Located the real structure.** §927 recorded "the frame difference is 2 extra callee-saved registers".
This round found **where the reference's `ebx`/`edi` live**: saved once at `0x1000282c`, ~190 bytes into the
function, and restored at **four** sites (`0x10002dac`, `0x10002de5`, `0x10002e17`, `0x10002e49`), each
immediately after `call dword ptr [0x10024010]` (`CloseHandle`) and each ending `pop edi; pop ebx;
jmp 0x10002e66`. Ours saves both in the prologue and emits one interleaved epilogue.

So the difference is not a prologue shape but a **liveness window bounded by the four cleanup paths** —
which is what §81's two named levers ("deferred `push ebx; push edi` at 0x1000282c", "`pCtx->Esp` parked in
ebx from 0x10002931") describe, now with the restore count and their common target pinned down. →
allocator Finding 66.

**Self-caught error mid-round.** I first read the `push ebx`/`push edi` at `0x1000287e` and `0x10002cdc` as
further deferred saves and reported "9 paired save/restore sites". They are **call arguments** —
`push ebp; call edi` at `0x1000287f`, `push eax; call [0x10024014]` at `0x10002ce5`. Corrected before
recording. `instr_diff.py`'s own output ("ref-only x33: push ADDR") is what made the argument/save
distinction worth checking at all.

**Not landed.** The carrier is at its span (2128, verified), and §81 already records 8 declaration

## Round 993 — CrashDump's deferred save is a register-ROLE swap; the header's −2 is +30

Round 992 found the reference saves `ebx`/`edi` at `0x1000282c` instead of in the prologue. This round found
**why**, and it is not a save placement:

| | reference | ours |
|---|---|---|
| `hDbgFile` (CreateFileA result) | **ebp** — `mov ebp,eax` @0x1000281d | **edi** — `mov edi,eax` @0x1000281f |
| save pair | `push ebx; push edi` @0x1000282c | prologue |

The reference parks `hDbgFile` in **ebp** and keeps **edi** free for its own later use (`mov edi,[0x10024034]`
then `call edi`). We hold `edi` from byte ~0xAF, so msvc6 saves it at entry. → allocator Finding 67.

**Probe, reverted (byte-identical):** giving `hDbgFile` a tighter block-local scope so its live range ends
before the walk measures **+0** — msvc6 folds the alias and keeps the allocation. The register role is not
C-steerable, consistent with §1.

**Header correction (fourth stale delta in four rounds).** `CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter.c:139-142`
records a round-129 lane claiming moving `nFrames = 0x800;` before the walk loop gives **−2**. Applied exactly
as written: **+30** (residue 8,628 → 8,658). Reverted. The note's `1597 -> 1595` predates the round-110 span
fix; the carrier now sits at 1,583. → allocator Finding 67, workflow-traps §14.

```

REF B @0x1000ef7b  pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp; xor eax,eax; pop ebx; add esp,0xc; ret  <- 1 branch
```

Our surviving epilogue is **byte-identical to B** — so it is a *missing copy*, not wrong code. This is the
cleanest instance yet: the earlier three involve byte-identical epilogues, so the exits themselves could be
suspected; here they provably differ by five bytes and msvc6 still folds them. → codegen-walls §2 addendum.

structure still folds all three exits).

epilogue-merge carrier immediately. That is worth running before probing *any* carrier, since it separates

## Round 1004 — register pressure matches on 18 of 19 carriers; the class is pure register choice

Tested the assumption behind the 67.5% register-role classification (round 1003): is the difference in *which*
register a value receives, or in *how many* the function needs? Only the second is C-addressable, since it is
live-range pressure.

**Measured the callee-saved save sequence on all 19 carriers, reference vs ours: 18 are identical, including
save ORDER.** (`ebx ebp esi edi` on most; `gm_AllocGebaeude` and `m_AllocTracked` `ebp ebx esi edi`;
`gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` `esi ebx ebp edi`; `gm_ObjectsAvailble` `esi ebx edi ebp`; `gm_CalculateProductionValue`
`ebx esi ebp edi` — each matching its reference exactly.)

The single exception is `CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter`, whose cause is already isolated (Finding 67:
`hDbgFile` in `ebp` vs `edi`, which is what lets the reference defer the `ebx`/`edi` pair).

**So register pressure is already right on 18 of 19.** The 5,825 register-class bytes are not a "needs a
different number of registers" problem — they are the allocator choosing differently among registers it already
has. That is §1's class, now with the pressure dimension ruled out as the cause by measurement rather than
assumption. → allocator Finding 68.

**Self-caught measurement error.** My first reading took the first four `push` of any callee-saved register and
reported `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist` as `ebx ebp ebx ebx`. That is wrong — the later `push ebx` operands are call
*arguments*, not saves. Its real prologue is `push ebx; push ebp`, matching ours. Corrected before recording;
the method note is in the finding so the next reader does not repeat it.

## Round 1005 — branch_census.py overstates structural difference; ServerMainThread's "+340" is a pairing artifact

Tested the `place` class (19.4% of residue) by examining `ServerMainThread`'s 14 reported target-differing
branches. **Most are not structural differences.**

**The deltas are ±1..3, not different blocks:** `{-1 x5, -2 x5, -3 x3, +340 x1}`. Nine of fourteen are a
one-to-three-byte displacement drift — the branch reaches the same block, a few bytes off.

**The `+340` outlier is a PAIRING artifact.** Aligning by index pairs the wrong instructions once the streams
desynchronise by one:

```
reference  0x100098e3  je  0x100097c5    (esi == 0 -> loop back)
           0x100098e9  jmp 0x10009919    (else      -> exit)
ours       0x100098e5  jne 0x1000991a    (esi != 0 -> exit)
           0x100098e7  jmp 0x100097c5    (else      -> loop back)
```

Index alignment subtracts a *taken-branch* target from a *fallthrough* target and yields 340. **Decoded
properly the control flow is identical** — both images send `esi == 0` to `0x100097c5` and the other edge to the
exit block; the reference uses `je` + fallthrough, ours `jne` + fallthrough. That is §50's branch-polarity
class, and the exit targets differ by exactly 1 byte because our block is 1 byte shorter locally.

**What this changes.** `branch_census.py`'s count is an **upper bound** on structural difference, not a
measurement — it counts branches whose *encoding* differs, including polarity and drift. The round-971 table
(`gm_AllocSpieler` 21, `ServerMainThread` 14, `cm_ExSellObjekt` 7, …) should be read that way. §13's four-class
classifier survives, because what it actually uses is the split at **zero**: the eight carriers with no
target-differing branches are genuinely zero. → measure-traps §27.

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK. No source edit; no baseline moved.

## Round 1006 — built a correct CFG comparator (six attempts, five rejected); the honest `place` number

`branch_census.py` overstates structural difference (§27), so this round built the replacement properly.
Getting there took six formulations; five were wrong and each looked plausible. All six are recorded in
measure-traps §28 — the failures are the useful part, because four of them were caught only by a check I
had to think to run.

**The killer was #5, BFS canonical labelling.** A labelling derived from a traversal is *not* canonical:
visiting a node's two successors in the other order changed **452 edges on the same reference graph**. It
looks correct — deterministic, standard, stable for identical input — and it over-reported
`gm_AllocSpieler` as having 187-214 differing edges against a block-kind histogram matching within 2 nodes.

**The two guards now shipped in the tool:**

| guard | catches |
|---|---|
| `--self-test` | an always-zero tool: redirects one branch in an in-memory copy of the build and asserts the canonical form changes |
| order-swap invariant test | a non-canonical labelling: shuffle the input dicts on the SAME graph; the canonical form must not change |

**Result — the first trustworthy number for the `place` class:**

| verdict | carriers |
|---|---|
| **SAME control-flow shape** (7) | `ServerMainThread`, `m_AllocTracked`, `srv_LoadBuf`, `gm_ObjectsAvailble`, `vfs_ReadCompressed`, `cm_ExProdObjekt`, `gm_CalculateProductionValue` |
| **DIFFERS** (12) | the rest, profile delta 1-2 blocks each |

`ServerMainThread` reading **SAME** is the headline: `branch_census.py` called it 14 target-differing branches,
round 1005 hand-decoded one as a pairing artifact, and the correct tool says its control flow is identical.
Also hand-verified `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` (reference `jcc 19, ret 5, jmp 1` vs ours `jcc 20, ret 5` — one
`jmp` became a `jcc`) so the tool is not merely permissive.

**What this changes.** The `place` class (19.4% of residue, 1,675 bytes) splits into 7 carriers whose control
flow is already correct — so their residual is drift/encoding, not structure — and 12 with a real shape
difference of 1-2 blocks. That is a **smaller and more precise** structural component than the index-based
census implied, and it is the first version of this measurement that survives both guards.

## Round 1007 — round 1006's CFG tool was wrong; replaced with exact isomorphism (two more bugs found)

Round 1006 shipped `cfg_compare.py` and reported 7 carriers with identical control flow. **That verdict was
unsound**, and this round found out why by stress-testing the tool instead of using it.

**The coarse canonical form is provably too blunt.** Exhaustive search over all CFGs of 3 nodes (2,197 graphs):
**272,473 non-isomorphic pairs it reports as equal.** The form was block-kind multiset + degree profile +
edge-kind multiset, which cannot distinguish graphs that differ only in *where* an edge attaches among
same-kind, same-degree nodes.

**Replacing it surfaced two more bugs, each of which had produced a confident wrong answer:**

| bug | symptom | fix |
|---|---|---|
| comparing WL-1 colour **IDs** across graphs | unmutated build read *non*-isomorphic to the reference for every carrier | `_wl1` interns to dense ids per call; compare the class-size multiset instead |
| backtracking with only an `a in mapping` test | `ServerMainThread` non-isomorphic despite identical WL-1 partitions | recurse over a flat (colour, node) slot list so a class is not re-entered |

**The corrected answer, verified three ways.** `gm_AllocSpieler` and `ServerMainThread` — both SAME in round
1006 — are genuinely DIFFERS. For `gm_AllocSpieler` the block kinds differ directly
(`ref jcc 136/jmp 26` vs `bld jcc 134/jmp 28`). For `ServerMainThread` every aggregate matches (kinds,

## Round 1010 — round 1009's mechanism was wrong: it is test ORDER + arity, not polarity

Round 1009 concluded that `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity`'s one-block CFG difference was shapes §50's
branch-polarity class. **That was wrong**, and testing it directly showed why.

**The undirected-edge count differs** (reference 36, ours 37), so the graphs are not related by a polarity
swap alone. The out-degree histograms over the same 25 blocks give the mechanism:

| | out-degree 2 | out-degree 1 | out-degree 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference | 19 | **1** | 5 |
| ours | **20** | **0** | 5 |

Decoding both loop tails in full shows the reference runs the **sentinel test (`cmp eax,edx`) first**, then the
hit test; ours runs the **hit test (`cmp eax,ebp`) first**. The swap changes the exit edge's **arity** — an
unconditional `jmp` in the reference, a second `jcc` in ours. That is §84's statement-order class, not §50.
→ codegen-walls §17, corrected in place with the mechanism written out.

**Probe on the corrected mechanism:** `list_cursor++; elem = list_cursor[1]; if (elem == 0) break; if (elem ==
type) ...` (sentinel test moved first) measures **+243** (residue 8,628 → 8,873). Reverted. The file header's
account holds — *"the entry compare is load-bearing for correctness"*.

| probe (this carrier) | result |
|---|---|
| invert the sentinel test's polarity (`!= 0 continue`) | +0, byte-identical |
| `list_cursor++; elem = *list_cursor;` | +228 |
| move the sentinel test first | **+243** |

All three reverted; baseline rebuilt and verified at 8,628.

**Process note worth keeping.** Two consecutive rounds (1009, 1010) reached opposite conclusions about the same
16 bytes, because 1009 reasoned from the *shape* of the difference and 1010 *measured* it (undirected edge
count + out-degree histograms). The measurement took one command. This is the same failure the round-978/979
pair had: inferring a mechanism from a summary statistic instead of decoding the region.

## Round 1012 — address-based isomorphism was the wrong primitive; `ServerMainThread` is a 2-of-280 near-miss

Round 1011 classified `ServerMainThread` as the tree's only "merge-class" carrier, from its neighbourhood
profiles. **That was an artifact**, and this round found the cause by changing the comparison primitive.

**Compared under a block correspondence by instruction ordinal** (k-th instruction of the reference ↔ k-th of
ours) instead of by address: **278 of 280 successor pairs match**. The two that differ are the pair hand-verified
back in round 1005 at `0x100098e3`/`0x100098e9` — `je 0x100097c5` + `jmp 0x10009919` against
`jne 0x1000991a` + `jmp 0x100097c5`: same two destinations, swapped polarity.

So `ServerMainThread` is **polarity-only on 2 of 280 edges**, which is what round 1005 said. Rounds 1010's
"arity" reading and 1011's "merge" reading were both artifacts of comparing **addresses**: our blocks sit 2-3
bytes earlier, so their targets land on different addresses for a reason downstream of an encoding choice.

**The tool now reports a graded verdict, `mismatches / edges-checked`:**

| carrier | differing edges by ordinal |
|---|---|
| `ServerMainThread` | **2 / 280 (0.7%)** |
| `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist` | 6 / 30 |
| `vfs_OpenStream` | 7 / 27 |
| `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` | 9 / 10 |
| `gm_AllocSpieler` | 75 / 132 |
| `m_AllocTracked`, `srv_LoadBuf`, `gm_ObjectsAvailble`, `vfs_ReadCompressed`, `cm_ExProdObjekt`, `gm_CalculateProductionValue` | **0** |

→ measure-traps §31; codegen-walls §18 carries a dated correction over the superseded merge reading.

**Three rounds, one root cause.** 1009, 1010 and 1011 each named a different mechanism for the same bytes
(polarity → arity → merge) because each reasoned from a summary the previous round had computed with the wrong
primitive. The fix was not a better inference but a better comparison: establish the block correspondence
first, then compare the induced edges.

## Round 1014 — ServerMainThread's last 2 edges are loop-polarity, not steerable from C

Acted on round 1013's isolation: `ServerMainThread`'s entire control-flow difference is **2 of 280 edges**, a
polarity swap on the same two destinations (`0x100097c5` continue / `0x10009919` exit).

The reference encodes the **taken** edge as the loop-continuing one (`test esi,esi` / `je continue` / `jmp exit`);
we encode the exiting one as taken (`jne exit` / `jmp continue`).

**Three source spellings compiled, all byte-identical (+0):**

| spelling | delta |
|---|---|
| `} while (!(phase_complete != 0));` | **+0** |
| `if (phase_complete) break; } while (1);` | **+0** |
| inner scan as `for (;;) { if (phase_complete == 0) break; ... }` | **+0** |

A fourth attempt was malformed and did not compile — not a valid probe, recorded as such.

**msvc6 canonicalises loop-condition polarity**: it decides which edge is the taken branch from the loop's
shape, not from the spelling of the C condition. → codegen-walls §19.

**This closes `ServerMainThread`'s control-flow lane.** Its CFG differs from the reference in exactly 2 branch
*encodings* out of 280 edges, both polarity, and that polarity is not addressable from C89. Its 367 residual
bytes are therefore block-placement and register-role work, consistent with its existing classification, not a
structural defect.

## Round 1017 — re-tested the "no slack" conclusion by trying to falsify it; it holds, and round 990's arithmetic was unsound

Tried to falsify my own claim that no carrier has size headroom, by looking for removable bytes rather than
accepting the span measurement.

**Screened all 19 carriers for span slack** (COMDAT raw vs next-tracked-VA span): **zero have slack**; 167 objects
are exactly at span and 6 are under. No carrier can accept a size-increasing edit.

**`gm_AllocSpieler`'s "119 bytes of padding" was an arithmetic artifact.** Round 990 computed
`span - sum(instruction sizes)` and got 119 because the linear decoder stopped early. The sound test:

```
reference  1063 instructions summing to 3696   (span 3696, remainder 0)
built      1061 instructions summing to 3696   (span 3696, remainder 0)
```

Both decoders consume the span exactly, so there is no padding. Our stream has **two fewer instructions**,
offset by larger encodings — that is what the 2,823-byte residue consists of, not a size deficit. Both tails are
byte-identical (`ret` + 7 nops ending at `0x100196c0`). → measure-traps §34.

**This makes the constraint precise rather than vague.** The carrier is not "16 bytes short of room"; it is a
fixed 3,696-byte span containing the same instruction sequence with 2 fewer instructions and different register
encodings. Any fix must be **size-neutral** — which is why every size-increasing probe across rounds 990-1002
collapsed the composition.

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK. No source edit; no baseline moved.

## Round 1018 — round 1017 was wrong: there IS headroom, and cm_ExProdObjekt's "15 bytes" was right

Round 1017 concluded "slack 0" on every carrier by comparing the COMDAT **raw** size against the span. That is
self-fulfilling — msvc6 pads the COMDAT to the span with trailing `nop`s, so the two are equal by construction
and the comparison measures the pad, not our code.

**The correct measure is our code up to and including the final `ret`:**

| carrier | reference code | our code | span | **real headroom** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cm_ExProdObjekt` | 1008 | **993** | 1008 | **15** |
| `ServerMainThread` | 2434 | 2434 | 2448 | 14 |
| `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState` | 1463 | 1460 | 1472 | 12 |
| `CrashDump` | 2115 | 2120 | 2128 | 8 |
| `cm_ExSellObjekt` | 2057 | 2056 | 2064 | 8 |
| `gm_AllocSpieler` | 3689 | 3689 | 3696 | 7 |
| `srv_LoadBuf` | 750 | 750 | 752 | 2 |

`cm_ExProdObjekt`'s recorded `size = 993` confirms it: the reference is 1008, we emit 993, and 15 bytes are
available. **Its header's "15 bytes of unused slack" was correct**, and round 1016's dismissal of that claim as
stale was wrong.

**Three methods, three answers — only the third sound:**

| method | answer | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `span - sum(sizes)` after a truncated decode (990) | 119 | over-counts |
| COMDAT raw vs span (1001, 1017) | 0 | self-fulfilling: measures the pad |
| last non-`nop` end vs span (1018) | 2-15 | **correct** |

→ measure-traps §34, corrected in place.

**What this changes.** The "every carrier is exactly at span, so only size-neutral edits can land" constraint —
which I have repeated for many rounds and used to justify rejecting probes — is **false**. Size-increasing edits
of up to 15 bytes are available on `cm_ExProdObjekt`, 14 on `ServerMainThread`, and 7-12 on most others. That
reopens a class of probes I had been filtering out.

(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK. No source edit; no baseline moved.

## Round 1020 — the aliasing lever was the last untried spelling on cm_ExProdObjekt; it is a wall, +658

Shapes §44 makes `#pragma optimize("a", on)` the lever for "a pure transposition of a load and a store to
the same object". `cm_ExProdObjekt` has exactly that signature — ref loads `g_unknown_1de450` at
`0x1000e20c` before the volatile dead store, we emit it after — and shapes §60 had closed every
source-order spelling. The aliasing switch was therefore the one lever never tried on this row, and the
`/Oa` screen in the carrier table (TODO:23260) covers the other eighteen carriers, not this one.

Measured both spellings at the link:

| form | object | linked | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline `/Ox /Gd` | 2897 | 21 | — |
| `#pragma optimize("a", on)` | — | 679 | **+658** |
| `/Oa` on the compile line | 2881 | 679 | **+658** |

The two agree byte for byte: the pragma and `/Oa` are the same switch. `/Ow` is inert (object 2897).

**Why §44 does not transfer.** §44's verified site (`sim_AdvanceGameClock`) has *one* transposition, so
switching the assumption off fixes it and nothing else moves. `cm_ExProdObjekt` has three residual clusters
plus a large loop; the switch re-schedules all of them, and the bytes it fixes cost 658. **Cluster count is
the gate on the `"a"` lever.**

## Round 1023 — round 1022's "50 hidden functions / fn4 is 514 bytes" is wrong: it is 10 functions

Round 1022 split the twelve over-wide discovery spans at every `ret` (`0xc3`) and got 51 sibling
functions, with "fn4" at `0x1000db5d` (1230 B) carrying 514 of the 694 raw-link bytes. **Both numbers are
wrong**, and the method that produced them is unsound.

**Why.** In these spans most `ret`s are **branch targets** — return sites inside one larger function. Split
on `ret` and a single multi-return function becomes several phantom "functions".

Checked `0x1000db5d`, round 1022's headline lever: **not a function start at all.** The bytes immediately
before it are `... 5f 5e 5d 5b 81 c4 28 02 00 00 c3` — a complete `add esp,0x228; ret` epilogue — and
`0x1000db5d` opens `39 7e 23 74 17` (`cmp [esi+0x23],edi; je ...`), which continues an expression already
in progress. Nothing in the image references `0x1000db5d`.

**The sound test.** A start needs three conditions together: preceded by `90` padding; **not** targeted by
any `e8`/`e9`/`eb`/`7x`/`0f 8x` branch anywhere in the image; and a plausible msvc6 prologue. Applied to all
twelve spans:

| confirmed start | span | prologue |
|---|---|---|
| `0x1000d340` | `0x1000cfe0` | `mov eax,imm` |
| `0x1000d730` | `0x1000d6e0` | `sub esp,imm8` |
| `0x1000d930` | `0x1000d8a0` | `sub esp,imm32` |
| `0x1000e750` | `0x1000e690` | `mov eax,[abs]` |
| `0x1000e9c0` | `0x1000e8d0` | `push edi` |
| `0x1000f480`, `0x1000f590` | `0x1000f3b0` | `sub esp,imm8` / `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x1000fad0` | `0x1000f980` | `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x10010080` | `0x10010010` | `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x10010140` | `0x100100a0` | `mov eax,[abs]` |

**10 functions, not 51.** `0x1000d330` and `0x10010260` hold only padding after their first function.

Corroboration on the known case: `cm_MarkAndReturn` (`0x1000d330`) is EXACT at 14 bytes, and its "sibling"
is `90 90 | b8 01 00 00 00 c3` — a genuine second function, referenced from nowhere. That one is real; it
is also the only case where `ret+1` coincides with a function start.

**One number survives.** The 694 raw-link bytes for the twelve spans were measured by byte compare over the
whole span, not by the split, so that total stands. Only its *attribution* to 51 functions and to "fn4" was
wrong. The largest single span is `0x1000d8a0` at 569 bytes, and it is **one** function of 2064 bytes
starting at `0x1000d930` (ends `pop esi; ret` before the pad at `0x1000e74f`), not six.

Corrections applied to `docs/general-knowledge.md` in place. **No source, metadata or `build.make` change
was made this round; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

> **CORRECTED by round 1023.** The per-sibling table below is unsound: it split spans at every `ret`, but

> functions**, and "fn4" at `0x1000db5d` is not a function start at all. The **694-byte total stands**

## Round 1024 — the missing ten have a root cause: a pad threshold of 3 in the discoverer

Round 1023 established there are 10 missing sibling functions, not 51. This round found **why** they are
missing, and it is a one-line defect, not a discovery limit.

**Root cause.** `rebrew/discover.py::_capstone_sweep` step 2 promotes a candidate only when the preceding
padding run is `>= 3` bytes:

```python
if j - i >= 3 and j < n:
    starts.add(va_base + j)
```

All ten missing starts are preceded by **1 or 2** `90` bytes — measured, every one — so that step drops
them. Steps 3 and 4 do not recover them: they use prologues other than `55 8b ec` (`81 ec`, `83 ec`, `a1`,
`8b 44`, `b8`, `33 c9`, `5x`) and are reached only through tables or not at all.

| missing start | pad before | prologue |
|---|---|---|
| `0x1000d340` | 2 | `mov eax,imm` |
| `0x1000d730` | 2 | `sub esp,imm8` |
| `0x1000d930` | 2 | `sub esp,imm32` |
| `0x1000e750` | 1 | `mov eax,[abs]` |
| `0x1000e9c0` | 1 | `push edi` |
| `0x1000f480` | 2 | `sub esp,imm8` |
| `0x1000f590` | 1 | `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x1000fad0` | 1 | `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x10010080` | 2 | `mov eax,[esp+x]` |
| `0x10010140` | 1 | `mov eax,[abs]` |

**Re-discovery is not a workaround.** Re-ran `rebrew discover-functions` and got the identical 543 entries.
`--min-size 4` gives 565 and still contains none of the ten. The merge is deterministic.

**The fix, measured on the binary.** Lowering the threshold to 1 alone adds **380** starts, nearly all
mid-instruction `90` bytes. Threshold 1 **plus** (a) not-a-branch-target and (b) a valid prologue gives
**820** starts from 800 — all ten recovered, 20 new candidates instead of 380.

**Not applied:** rebrew here is an installed wheel (`rebrew-2.5.0.dist-info`), not a checkout, so there is
no source tree to patch. Written up as workflow-traps §17 with the root cause, the measured fix and the
false-positive count. Also carried into `docs/general-knowledge.md`.

**Also corrected this round:** `docs/workflow-traps.md` §16 still asserted "slack is 0, not 15" and told
future rounds to assume 0. That was round 998's claim, repeated by round 1017, and disproved by round 1018 —
the check behind it (`object .text raw == span`) is tautological because msvc6 pads the COMDAT to the span.
§16 now records the correct measure and the correct conclusion (headroom is capacity, not affordance).

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1026 — the graded residue and the raw-link residue are an exact partition: 8628 + 5081, zero overlap

Decomposed `.text`'s 0x22846 bytes across three artifacts, comparing every offset in the reference, the raw
link (`build/split_poc.dll`) and the shipped file (`build/server.dll`):

| class | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| raw differs, shipped matches | **5,081** | postlink supplied the reference byte |
| raw differs, shipped differs | **8,628** | the graded residue |
| raw matches, shipped differs | **0** | postlink introduces nothing |

`8628 + 5081 = 13,709` — the raw link's total divergence, exactly. Two consequences:

- **Postlink is a pure repair step.** The shipped-only class is empty, so it never corrupts a byte the build
  got right. The graded residue is precisely the subset of the production gap it could not repair.
- **The 8,628 is a subset of the 13,709.** Every graded-residue byte is also wrong in the raw link, so the two
  rulers agree on *which* carriers fail even though they disagree on magnitude. A round may study a carrier on
  the raw link and score it on the shipped file without the two contradicting each other.

**Worked example of the 5,081 class, at `0x10015f80` (inside `gm_ObjectsAvailble`).** Reference and shipped
both read `mov eax,[0x1014d8c0]` (`g_entity_ptr`); the raw link reads `mov eax,[0x11766ae8]`, because our
`link_stubs.c:198` stub is placed at `0x11766ae8` while the reference's symbol lives at `0x1014d8c0`. Postlink
rewrites the operand, so **the shipped byte is already correct and this is not residue**. A round studying
that offset on the raw link would chase a plausible-looking wrong global that cannot be fixed by editing the
definition.

**Two of my own errors, corrected in place while writing this up:**

1. I first read `0x10015f80` as `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity`'s real entry because the prologue bytes
   `a1 c0 d8 14 10 56 32 c9` occur there. They do — but `0x10015f80` is inside `gm_ObjectsAvailble`
   (`0x10015f70`, 720 bytes, ends `0x10016240`), and the match is a false positive.
2. `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` genuinely starts at `0x10016f80` (inventory `fcn.10016f80`, 352 bytes), and
   its first bytes `c4 08 5e c3` + ten `90`s are **identical on both sides** — that is the shared epilogue
   tail the layout leaves at the entry. Its prologue begins at `0x10016f8a`. So there is no divergence in its
   first 16 bytes, and `fault_address.py`'s other 18 rows all reproduce.

Both recorded in measure-traps §37, which also states the operative rule: **check the shipped image before
treating a raw-link operand difference as work.**

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1027 — gm_FindNextFilteredEntity: the entry reorder reproduces the reference's instruction order and still scores +6

Round 1026's decomposition pointed at `0x10015f80`/`0x10016f80`. Walking the two streams from
`gm_FindNextFilteredEntity`'s entry (`0x10016f80`, 352 B) with capstone, aligned on address, the third
instruction disagrees:

```
ref  mov eax, [0x1014d8c0]; push esi; xor cl, cl; lea esi,[eax+0xa900]; mov eax,[0x100a8c30]; test eax,eax
bld  mov eax, [0x1014d8c0]; push esi; test eax,eax; je 0x100170d6; lea esi,[eax+0xa900]; mov eax,[0x100a8c30]
```

The reference forms `end` before testing `g_entity_type_table`; ours tests the table first. That is a
statement-order divergence — the class the objective says to attack first — so three spellings were
measured, **at the link**, all reverted:

| variant | link delta |
|---|---|
| `match = 0; end = ...; if (table == 0) return 0;` (reorder the guard below `end`) | **+6** |
| `end = ...; if (table == 0) return 0; if (dynasty > 0x100) return 0; match = 0;` | **+6** |
| `end` split into a braced block with its own `entity_base` temp, guard left in place | **+6** |

**The result worth keeping is not the +6, it is that variant 1 worked and did not pay.** Verified by
re-disassembling the recomposed image: the reorder moved `lea esi,[eax+0xa900]` from instruction **5 to
instruction 2**, which is exactly where the reference has it, and the fault instruction count still moved
by +6. So the cost is downstream of the fault and larger than the local gain — **a carrier can have a fault
whose removal is not a win.**

Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §21, with the corollary: the fault-instruction identity is a *diagnostic*,
not a target. Score at the link before treating a fault-match as progress.

**Also from this round:** `fault_address.py`'s `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` row was checked against the
streams and is correct — my round-1026 note calling it "the wrong span" was wrong and is corrected. The
bytes at `0x10016f80` being a shared epilogue tail is normal; the prologue is at `0x10016f8a`, inside the
function.

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

| carrier | idx | reference | ours | kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gm_AllocSpieler` | 48 | `lea edx,[edx+0x100358fc]` | `mov [ebp],bx` | reorder |
| `CrashDump` | 0 | `sub esp,0x280` | `sub esp,0x284` | frame size |
| `cm_ExSellObjekt` | 14 | `mov [esp+0x14],edi` | `mov [esp+0x24],edi` | slot |
| `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState` | 26 | `jle` | `jle` (target -2) | branch target |
| `cm_ExCopyEntityData` | 19 | `jne` | `jne` (target -2) | branch target |
