| `gm_AllocGebaeude` | 38 | `mov edx,[0x10030b6c]` | `mov [ebp-0xc],eax` | reorder |
| `vfs_OpenStream` | 18 | `cmp byte [eax],0` | `mov al,[eax]` | fold |
| `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` | 2 | `xor cl,cl` | `test eax,eax` | reorder (**+6**, round 1027) |
| `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist` | 66 | `lea edx,[eax+eax*8]` | `lea eax,[eax+eax*8]` | dest register |
| `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` | 8 | `xor ebp,ebp` | `mov [esp+0x18],0x12` | statement order |
| **`m_AllocTracked`** | **6** | **`push esi`** | **`cmp eax,ebx`** | **pure adjacent swap** |
| `srv_LoadBuf` | 26 | `push eax` | `mov [ebp+0x2c],ecx` | reorder |
| `gm_ObjectsAvailble` | 73 | `test ebx,ebx` | `test edi,edi` | register role |
| `vfs_ReadCompressed` | 65 | `mov edi,eax` | `test eax,eax` | reorder |
| `cm_ExProdObjekt` | 73 | `mov edx,[0x101de450]` | `mov ebx,[ebp+0x16]` | reorder (barrier) |
| `cm_ProcessCommandQueue` | 17 | `jne` | `jne` (target -4) | branch target |
| `gm_CalculateProductionValue` | 68 | `fxch st(1)` | `cmp byte [esi],0x17` | x87 fold |

**The best candidate on this table is `m_AllocTracked`**: a swap of **exactly two adjacent instructions**,
with `ref[6]==bld[7]` and `ref[7]==bld[6]` verified by decoding both streams, and the rest of the first 12
instructions byte-identical. Reference saves `esi` before the `g_array_ptr == 0` test; we test first.

Two source spellings measured at the link, both reverted:

| variant | link delta |
|---|---|
| swap the entry guards (`if (size == 0)` before `if (g_array_ptr == 0)`) | **+539** |
| hoist `node = &g_alloc_root_name;` above both guards | **+61** |

**Neither is close.** `push esi` is a callee-save placed by liveness; the `cmp` is a guard placed by source,
but moving it drags every dependent block. The header's existing "these 2 remaining target-only items are
allocator" verdict is now **independently confirmed**, and both spellings are retired rather than untried.
Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §22.

**The generalisation, now from two measured cases (this and §21):** a carrier whose fault is a *reorder* is
not automatically the best target even when the swapped pair is adjacent and the surrounding bytes match.
The reorder is a symptom of a liveness/scheduling decision, and reproducing it from source costs more than
the local gain.

**Sweep method note.** This table is a useful diagnostic because the *kind* of the differing instruction
suggests which lever to reach for (branch target -> §13 block placement; register-only -> allocator
Findings 62/63; `cmp`/`mov` fold -> shapes; reorder -> liveness, no C lever). It does not by itself order
the work, and the two reorders it flagged most favourably both cost.

## Round 1029 — gm_ObjectsAvailble: 220/235 identical, three new spellings, none lands; one "inert" claim is +4

`gm_ObjectsAvailble` (`0x10015f70`, 720 B, 25 residue) is the cleanest register-role carrier in the tree —
**220 of 235 instructions identical, instruction counts equal (235/235)**, with the 15 differences a pure
`ebx`↔`edi` exchange. Reference tests `slot_cursor` in `ebx` and holds `slot_base` in `edi`; ours is reversed.

Three spellings re-measured at the link, all reverted:

| spelling | header's label | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `slot_base = ...;` before `slot_cursor = 0;` (initialiser order) | inert | **+4** |
| `slot_cursor` declared after `slot_base` | "inert" | **+0** — label confirmed |
| `slot_base` given an early use above the branch | not listed | **+4** |

**The header's "inert" labels are right in kind, not always zero.** One is exactly 0; the other is +4.
Recorded as allocator Finding 69 and, as a process rule, workflow-traps §18: an "inert" label means "already
tried", not "neutral under the current object", and it must be re-measured when a candidate stacks it with
another edit.

**The cheaper diagnostic, and what actually closed the row:** two *different* reorderings both landed on
exactly **+4**. Identical deltas from different edits is the signature of a **collapse** — the compiler
canonicalised both into one schedule, so the thing being varied is not a lever. That, plus 220/235 identity
and exact instruction-count parity, is a stronger closure argument than the sign of any single number.

## Round 1030 — the raw link's wrong global operands are by design; postlink's rewrite is complete (4398/4398)

Started from §22's `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState` diff, which showed our stream emitting
`cmp dword ptr [0x100373c4],0x10047` where the reference has `[0x1002d4ec]`. Same instruction, same
immediate, different global — which reads as a wrong-symbol defect in our source.

**It is not.** Traced to `src/link_stubs.c:81-82`:

```c
// DATA: SERVER 0x1002d4ec
int g_file_version = 0;
```

The `// DATA:` comment is **documentation for the tooling, not a placement directive** — no `#pragma
section`, no linker ordering key. The linker places the stub wherever its COMDAT ordering puts it and
`rebrew postlink --layout` rewrites every `.text` operand back to the reference address.

| artifact | dwords equal to `0x1002d4ec` | equal to the stub placement `0x100373c4` |
|---|---|---|
| reference | 23 | 0 |
| raw link (`split_poc.dll`) | 0 | 37 |
| shipped (`server.dll`) | 23 | 0 |

**The rewrite is complete.** Compared every dword in `.text` whose value lies in the data range
(`0x10024000..0x11768000`) between the reference and the shipped file: **4398 present in both, 0
mismatched.**

**Two dead ends this round, both worth recording so they are not repeated:**

1. **Removing the stray duplicate definition does not change it.** `gv_CheckSlotActive.c` carried an
   unannotated `int g_file_version;` shadowing the canonical declaration — removed, link-tested **+0**,
   reverted. Then nine `spiel*.c` files each carry `int g_current_year;` (canonical `0x10035880`), and all
   nine were removed and link-tested together: **+0**, reverted. Both are hygiene, not codegen, because
   postlink overwrites the operands regardless of which definition the linker picks.
2. **The `g_current_year` count looked like a defect and is not.** The reference has 17 `.text` dwords
   equal to `0x10035880`; the raw link has 9. But the 8 "missing" sites are in functions that read the
   global through a different operand form, not mis-bound — confirmed by locating every site in both
   images. A count difference between two images is only a finding after the sites are located, which is
   measure-traps §24's rule in its operand form.

**Recorded as `general-knowledge.md`** (placement architecture + the 4398/4398 measurement), which also
adds the third trap to the raw-link family: measure-traps §35 (raw vs shipped answer different questions),
§36 (do not assume a carrier's VA), and now **a wrong data operand in the raw link is not evidence of a
wrong symbol in the source** — it is the designed intermediate state and cannot be fixed by editing the
definition.

**No source change retained. No metadata or `build.make` change. Nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

| `gm_AllocGebaeude` | 263 | 223 | **1** | **1** |
| `vfs_OpenStream` | 170 | 102 | **1** | **1** |
| `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` | 82 | 75 | **1** | **1** |
| `gv_ExAllocGraveyardWorker` | 114 | 4 | 1 | 1 (unresolved — 4 matches) |

**Six carriers are a single displacement cliff**, so §109's framing is correct for them and the cliff is
the thing to attack. **`gm_AllocSpieler` is not one of them** — 4 values, 7 runs — which is where the
framing is weakest. A global-shift test on it also fails: best match 310/3519 at delta +5, chance level.

**This section's first draft reported `gm_AllocSpieler` as 12 runs / 10 values and concluded the wake
framing does not reproduce.** That was wrong — the image was sliced from the wrong origin. The corrected
table above reverses the headline: the framing reproduces for six carriers and fails only on the largest.
The error and its correction are both recorded in measure-traps §38, because the corrected version is the
more useful one: the profile is now a **triage tool** for choosing which carrier to attack.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

§38's table listed six carriers as "a single displacement cliff". Re-measured them with a **second, independent

## Round 1033 — a carrier has two first divergences: 11 of 19 disagree between the raw link and the shipped file

Rounds 1031-1032 built a displacement-profile triage tool on the raw link. This round asked a prior
question: **is the raw link's first divergence the same address as the shipped file's?** For every carrier,
walked both images against the reference from the carrier's entry:

| carrier | raw first diff | shipped first diff | bytes postlink corrected between |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gm_AllocSpieler` | `+0x6d` | `+0xaa` | 8 |
| `cm_ExSellObjekt` | `+0x7` | `+0x2c` | 3 |
| `gv_ExAllocGraveyardWorker` | `+0x6a` | `+0x107` | 10 |
| `ServerMainThread` | `+0x80` | `+0x3c7` | 4 |
| `gm_AllocGebaeude` | `+0xa` | `+0x60` | 8 |
| `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` | `+0x1` | `+0x6` | 4 |
| `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist` | `+0x38` | `+0xcc` | 20 |
| `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` | `+0x76` | `+0x83` | 3 |
| `m_AllocTracked` | `+0xa` | `+0x11` | 2 |
| `gm_ObjectsAvailble` | `+0x53` | `+0x10d` | 21 |
| `cm_ExProdObjekt` | `+0x4` | `+0xcd` | 21 |
| `gm_CalculateProductionValue` | `+0x6` | `+0xe4` | 23 |
| `CrashDump`, `ls_LoadBuildingEntityState`, `cm_ExCopyEntityData`, `vfs_OpenStream`, `srv_LoadBuf`, `vfs_ReadCompressed`, `cm_ProcessCommandQueue` | — | — | **agree** |

**Eleven of nineteen disagree**, and the raw link's divergence is always *earlier* — a 2-23 byte window of
data operands that postlink restores.

**Worked example, `gm_AllocSpieler`.** At `+0x6d` the raw link has `e4 65 76 11` (`0x117665e4`, our stub
placement); reference and shipped both have `34 54 03 10` (`0x10035434`). The streams are byte-identical
through `+0x90`, so **the raw link reports a divergence at `+0x6d` that the deliverable does not have.**

**Why this matters for method.** §35 recommends the raw link as the capability ruler, and it is the only
way to see what the build produces. But every carrier's documentation is keyed by the **shipped file's**
fault, and `fault_address.py` measures the shipped file. So a round studying a carrier on the raw link lands
on a different, earlier, postlink-supplied address and can read it as the carrier's problem — which is
exactly the class of error rounds 1030 and 1032 each spent budget on.

**Recorded as measure-traps §40** with the operational rule: raw link for "does the build produce these
bytes", shipped file for "which byte is the carrier failing on", and never carry a raw-link fault address
into a doc lookup.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

## Round 1034 — gm_CheckInventoryCapacity: header's byte-identity claim verified exactly; the crux probe is inert

`gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` (`0x10019ed0`, 395 B, 97 residue — it lives inside the 16-function
`spiel622.c` object, so `rebrew test` cannot score it per-function). Its header claims:

> Everything from offset 0x8f to the end is byte-identical; the only remaining differences are the seven
> relocation slots and the 0x1a-0x8e block.

**Verified against the shipped file, exactly:**

```
differing bytes 97 of 395
first +0x13   last +0x8e
clusters: (0x13..0x1f), (0x30..0x8e)
inside 0x1a..0x8e : 90
outside           :  7, all at +0x13..+0x19
bytes past +0x8e  :  0
```

The seven outside the block are at `+0x13..+0x19` — the header's seven relocation slots — and **nothing
differs past `+0x8e`**. The claim is exact.

**The fault, decoded from both streams:** at prologue index 8 the reference has `xor ebp,ebp`
(`in_list = 0`) where ours has `mov dword ptr [esp+0x18],0x12` (`list[2]`). Our source already puts
`in_list = 0;` first, so the scheduler sinks the store below the following `list[]` initialisers.

**The crux probe, reverted (+0 at the link, carrier unchanged).** The header records the three invariants it
could not satisfy together — *ebp-first order*, *edi roles*, *list[7] from ebp* — and states "27 combos of
in_list/cap positions, declaration order, base removal, cap-late, in_list=cap all measured, none gives
ebp-first + edi + ebp-list7 together". I tested one combination it lists but describes as unreachable:
`in_list = 0;` **and** `cap = 0;` moved to the top, with `list[7]` sourced from `in_list` instead of `0`.

Result: **`+0` at the link, and the carrier still has 97 differing bytes with the identical fault at index 8.**
So the store is not moved by that spelling either. Measured, reverted, and it confirms the header rather than
extending it — the source order does not reach the schedule.

**Also confirmed this round:** the header's 9-slot read-position sweep, its 12-spelling address grid and its
10-declaration-order grid are more complete than anything I would devise for this row. `cm_ExSellObjekt`'s
neighbouring record is equally settled — after its −200 win the cliff "fragmented into four independent 1-4
byte accumulations, largest 163B", every cluster ≥48B is register allocation or intra-block scheduling, and
the last probe was "locally correct, globally losing". Both rows are documented walls.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change retained; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1035 — a call-target multiset audit produces phantom results in both directions

Tried a cheap "is any callee missing or wrong" screen: compare the multiset of `call` targets per carrier
between the reference and the built image. **The screen is invalid across any known divergence**, and this
round measured both failure directions.

**Direction 1 — phantom missing calls (`gm_AllocSpieler`).** The multiset reported the shipped file missing
three calls the raw link has:

| image | instructions | calls |
|---|---|---|
| reference | 1056 | 55 |
| raw link | 1054 | 55 |
| shipped | **1014** | **52** |

The shipped stream decodes to 42 fewer instructions, so it is desynced and its multiset is not comparable.
No call is missing. (measure-traps §24, in call-target form.)

**Direction 2 — phantom wrong callee (`vfs_OpenStream`).** The multiset showed the reference calling
`0x1001b0c0` (`crt_toupper`, real code) where we call `0x1002387d` (`.rdata`, zeros) — which reads as a
wrong symbol and would send a round hunting the C. It is the **+1 displacement** from §38's single-byte
cliff:

```
ref  +0x5f  call 0x1001b0c0   (e8 5c 20  at +0x3f)
ship +0x5f  push eax          (50        at +0x3f)
ship +0x60  call 0x1002387d   (e8 18 ..  at +0x40)
```

Our call *is* the reference's call, one byte later. The decoded target is garbage because the decoder began
the instruction one byte off. Nothing is wrong with the callee.

**A useful by-product:** the audit did correctly identify that the other 17 carriers' call multisets match
once the two known-desynced rows are discounted, and that the genuinely-aligned rows
(`ls_LoadBuildingEntityState`, `cm_ExCopyEntityData`, `gv_ExAllocGraveyardWorker`, `ServerMainThread`,
`gm_AllocGebaeude`, `ahm_ExAllocAlchemist`, `m_AllocTracked`, `srv_LoadBuf`, `gm_ObjectsAvailble`,
`vfs_ReadCompressed`, `cm_ExProdObjekt`, `cm_ProcessCommandQueue`, `gm_CalculateProductionValue`,
`gm_CheckInventoryCapacity`) show **no missing or extra call at all**. So no carrier is missing a call to a
function the reference invokes — a negative result that is worth having, since "the reconstruction forgot a
call" was the one structural failure mode this screen could have caught.

**Recorded as measure-traps §41**, with the rule: any comparison built on decoded instructions is valid only
where the streams are known to be aligned, and call-target multisets must not span a known divergence.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1036 — "compare the data operands" gives 0, 707 or 9,855 depending on the offset filter

Set out to re-verify round 1030's claim that postlink's `.text` operand rewrite is complete (0 mismatched of
4398). Re-asked it a looser way and got 707 — which looked like a contradiction. It is not: the three
numbers are three different populations, and only one is a set of operands.

| population | rule | size | mismatched |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — operands** | dword is a data address in **both** images | 4,398 | **0** |
| B — either image | data address in the reference **or** the shipped file | 5,105 | 707 |
| C — no filter | every offset where the two dwords differ | — | 9,855 |

**Round 1030's number is confirmed: population A is 4398 / 0 mismatched.** A and B/C disagree because a
dword read at an arbitrary offset usually straddles two instructions; if the surrounding bytes differ — which
they do throughout the residue — the straddling dword differs too, and classifies as a "data address" only
by coincidence. Those are not operands.

Recorded as measure-traps §42 with the rule: a byte-offset sweep is not an instruction sweep, and when a
looser re-measurement contradicts an earlier tight one, check whether the two count the same population
before believing either.

**Also verified:** postlink's `locality` pass reports **4 stale operands recovered** deterministically on
every run — `.text+0xae64`, `+0xae85`, `+0x11378`, `+0x12209`, all 4-byte data addresses inside
`cmp reg,imm32`. Every one lands correctly in the shipped file (`0x1009aca0`, `0x1009aca2`, `0x10139820`,
`0x1009b762`). `0x1009aca2` is **odd-aligned** — a byte-level comparison against a struct's second byte —
which is exactly why a 4-aligned generic sweep needs a second, locality-driven pass. The pass works as
designed; the four are not defects.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

`general-knowledge.md` entry is replaced. The tool-fix proposal is withdrawn.

**The second-order lesson, and it is the valuable part.** Both "missing function" findings were measured
against a proxy (`function_structure.json`, known to be discoverer-owned) without ever checking the
authoritative population — `rebrew verify`'s own annotation list — for the same VAs. **A claim that X is

## Round 1039 — full clean rebuild reproduces the deliverable byte-for-byte (MD5 confirmed)

Twenty rounds have reported residue 8628 without ever testing whether that number survives a **clean**
build rather than an incremental one. Tested it.

```
cmake --build build --clean-first     -> fails at POST_BUILD postlink, BY DESIGN
cmake --build build --target final    -> succeeds
cmp <pre-clean build/server.dll> build/server.dll   -> identical
md5sum                                               -> 3febd2c4ca080a3749c12d4bf7452fbe (both)
```

**Residue after the clean rebuild: 8628 (`0x21b4`), unchanged.**

**The `--clean-first` failure is measure-traps §17**, and the message names the reason:

```
error: postlink failed: built .text is not position-aligned with the reference —
only 4847/7463 layout-map entries validate (64.9%, minimum 90%).
.text VirtualSize built 0x221f6 vs reference 0x22846.
```

That `0x221f6` is the **plain CMake link**, which is not the deliverable. The deliverable is
`--target final`, which runs `scripts/split_link.sh` and then `postlink_residual.py`.

**Two properties follow, and they are what makes the baseline trustworthy:**

- **8628 is not an artefact of stale objects.** A clean rebuild from source produces the same bytes, so the
  residue is a property of the sources. Every per-carrier delta this session measured with
  `linktest.sh`/`split_link.sh` inherits that assurance.
- **The tree is reproducible by a fresh clone.** The only external inputs are the five stock LIBCMT archives
  in `.scratch/libcmt/`, extracted from the toolchain images as `split_link.sh`'s header documents.

Recorded in `general-knowledge.md` with the correct clean recipe, since the `--clean-first` failure has

## Round 1040 — falsified the "shared cause" hypothesis: in spiel622.c, 14 file-mates are exact and 2 carriers are not

Every round this session has treated the 18 carriers as 18 independent walls, but that was never *tested* —
and a common cause (a header, a preamble spelling, a flag, a codegen state) would mean one fix closes all 18
and the per-carrier documentation is a red herring. Tested it, twice.

**Test 1 — carriers are spread across 11 directories.** `spiel_c` 3, `command_c` 3, `server_c` 3, `game` 2,
one each in `Error_c`, `loadsave_c`, `friedhof_logic_c`, `vfs_c`, `alchemistry_logic_c`, `m_alloc_c`, plus
`spiel_dumpD.c`. No common TU, module or header set.

**Test 2 — file-mates of carriers are byte-identical.** Across all 30 multi-function files,
**130 of 137 functions (94.9%) are byte-identical.** The decisive cases:

| file | carriers | file-mates (all residue 0) |
|---|---|---|
| `spiel622.c` | `gm_CalculateProductionValue`, `gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` | **14 functions** |
| `spiel_dumpD.c` | `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` | **3 functions** |

Same translation unit, same headers, same flags, same object — and in `spiel622.c` **14 functions are
byte-identical while two are not.**

**What this rules out:** any explanation that is a property of the *environment* — header, include order,
`#pragma`, flag, toolchain state, shared type or struct layout — because those are common to every function
in the TU, including the 94.9% that match. **The residue is a property of each carrier's own code.**

**What it does not rule out:** that carriers share a *mechanism*. §13's four classes are exactly that, and
register-role rotation is one mechanism across eight carriers. What is falsified is a shared **cause**
reachable by one edit, not a shared **class**.

Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §23. The test itself is the cheapest high-value one run this session — two
`grep`s and a byte compare per file — and it closes the last structural hypothesis about the residue's shape.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

shipped file.

**Result: 18 of 19 frames match exactly.** `gm_AllocSpieler` `0x41c`, `cm_ExSellObjekt` `0x228`,
`ServerMainThread` `0x1e4`, `srv_LoadBuf` `0x2a0`, `m_AllocTracked` `0x118`, `gm_AllocGebaeude` `0x410`,

**What this sharpens.** The register-role rotations on the eight zero-branch carriers happen under a frame
that is already correct, so they are a pure colouring choice among equally-valid allocations, not a

**The one exception is already a wall.** `CrashDump`'s surplus is shapes §81: four independent routes to

## Round 1042 — tried to automate the stale-note audit; the regex found zero and invented two

Round 1041 found a genuinely stale frame note by **reading** (`vfs_OpenStream`: "ours is 8" when ours is
`0xc`). This round tried to automate that class: extract every `sub esp,0xNN` from each carrier's header and
compare it to the frame the binary emits.

**Two hits, both false positives, both the same mistake:**

| file | regex found | binary | the actual sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cm_ExCopyEntityData.c:73` | `0x10` | `0xc` | "drops one frame dword (`sub esp,0x10` -> `0xc`)" — **documents the change** |
| `cm_ExProdObjekt.c:221` | `0x14` | `0x10` | "widens the frame to `sub esp,0x14` and moves every esp displacement, scoring 815" — **a rejected probe** |

A carrier's header is a **probe history**: it records spells that were tried, values that were fixed, and
variants that lost. Quoting a number from it usually does *not* assert that number is current — often the
opposite, because the entry exists to say it was wrong or rejected.

**The audit is withdrawn.** One real stale note was found this session and it was found by reading; the
regex found none and invented two. Recorded as measure-traps §43 with the rule: a header's numbers are
evidence about the past, so an extraction must carry the surrounding polarity ("is" vs "was", "gives" vs
"scored", `->` for a change, "rejected/lost" for a retired probe). Default expectation for any extracted
figure should be "not current" until the sentence says otherwise.

**The frame survey itself still stands** (round 1041, allocator Finding 70): **18 of 19 carriers have the
reference's exact frame**, `CrashDump` being the only exception at `0x284` vs `0x280`, and that row is the
documented shapes §81 wall (+66 linked, row +58 when the frame was closed).

## Round 1045 — gm_AllocSpieler's +0xaa transposition is now fully enumerated; every point loses

Round 1044 measured the transposition from the opposite direction (+361). This round closed the middle of
the space — partial moves — and the complete cost map is:

| spelling | link delta |
|---|---|
| `*(slot+0x16c) = 0;` moved below the `memset` (one store) | **+3** |
| `*(slot+0x170) = 0;` moved below the `memset` (one store) | **+3** |
| both zero-stores moved below the `memset` | **+361** |
| `memset` hoisted above the id store and both zero-stores | **+368** |
| `memset` hoisted above the two zero-stores only | **+361** |
| explicit `int scaled = idx * 0x21c;` local | **+5** |
| explicit `char* fill = (char*)0x100358a4 + idx*0x21c;` | **+0** (inert) |

**Two structural facts fall out:**

1. **The two single-store moves give the *identical* delta (+3).** Different edits, same number — the
   collapse signature from workflow-traps §18. msvc6 canonicalised both into one schedule, so *which*
   zero-store is moved is not a degree of freedom; only *how many* is.
2. **Hoisting the `memset` costs ~365 whichever side it lands on** (+361, +368), while moving zero-stores
   costs ~3 per store for the first and +361 for the second. The halves are asymmetric: the `memset` is the
   expensive operand because hoisting it forces the scaled index to be rematerialised across the call —
   exactly §109's stated mechanism, now confirmed from five points rather than one.

**The transposition is fully enumerated and every point on it loses.** Cheapest perturbation +3, dearest
+368, and the only inert spelling is the one that does not touch the schedule at all. Recorded in
`codegen-walls.md` §24.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

## Round 1046 — gm_AllocSpieler's 2,823 bytes are FOUR clusters and they are not displaced code

The row is described as "132 distributed schedule steps, no cliff" and its residue as a "displacement wake".
Both suggest many small scattered differences. Measured, it is neither.

**Cluster structure (17 clusters at gap <= 8):**

| cluster | size | share |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x1a4..+0x5f6` | **1,107** | **39.2%** |
| `+0xa0d..+0xd72` | **870** | **30.8%** |
| `+0x6cf..+0x8db` | **525** | **18.6%** |
| `+0x607..+0x6c6` | 192 | 6.8% |
| `+0xaa..+0x125`, `+0x130..+0x177` | 124, 72 | 4.4%, 2.6% |
| `+0xdd0..+0xe33` | 100 | 3.5% |
| eleven small/singleton | 5-27 each | 2.0% |

**Four clusters hold 90% of the residue** — not 132 scattered steps.

**Rigid-displacement test:** for each big cluster, the single offset `delta` maximising byte-match against the
reference:

| cluster | best delta | match |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x1a4..+0x5f6` (1,107 B) | +5 | **17.0%** |
| `+0x6cf..+0x8db` (525 B) | −13 | **13.9%** |
| `+0x607..+0x6c6` (192 B) | −8 | 18.3% |
| `+0xaa..+0x125` (124 B) | −16 | 20.3% |

**No cluster is a displaced copy.** A shifted region would match near 100% at its own delta; these peak at
14-20%, chance level for x86 byte comparison. The large clusters are **genuinely different code**.

**Reconciliation.** Measure-traps §38 profiled 4 displacement values across 7 runs and §39 corrected it by
showing only 34.1% of the carrier's contexts are findable in the reference. This is that correction made
concrete: the findable 34% sits in the small clusters; the four large ones are the unfindable 66%.
**§109's mechanism for the `+0xaa` fault stands** (round 1045 enumerated its whole perturbation space); its
extrapolation to the remaining bytes does not.

**So the row needs four independent local fixes, not one** — and only the first cluster's neighbourhood has
been probed (six spellings, all losing). The other three have no probe on record. Recorded as
`codegen-walls.md` §25, with the ordering note: future work on this row should go by cluster size, not by
fault address.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

## Round 1047 — corrected round 1046: the two biggest clusters ARE displacement; the test was byte-level

Round 1046 concluded `gm_AllocSpieler`'s clusters are "not displaced code" from a byte-level rigid-offset
test (best match 17.0% / 13.9%). **That conclusion was wrong**, and the error was granularity.

Re-measured by comparing **instruction streams with every `0x...` normalised to `A`**, so branch and data
displacements are not counted as differences:

| cluster | bytes | ref insns | our insns | equal modulo address |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `+0x1a4..+0x5f6` | 1,107 | 323 | 322 | **251/322 = 78.0%** |
| `+0xa0d..+0xd72` | 870 | 248 | 247 | **177/247 = 71.7%** |
| `+0x6cf..+0x8db` | 525 | 157 | 157 | 79/157 = 50.3% |

**The two large clusters are displaced code**, at 78% and 72% with instruction counts within 1. The byte test
failed because **every differing branch displacement breaks byte-window matching** — a window spanning a
`jne rel32` cannot match at any offset once the target moves, and branch displacements are dense in this
loop-heavy code. So the byte match rate collapsed to chance precisely on the best-aligned regions.

**A second artefact found and corrected in the same pass.** One 192-byte cluster reported **1 reference
instruction vs our 52**, which reads as a 51-instruction surplus and a strong probe candidate. It is a
**capstone desync**: the reference's first bytes there are `24 83` (`and al,0x83`), after which the decoder
stops emitting valid instructions. The raw bytes are ordinary code. **A near-zero count is a desync, not a
surplus.**

Both recorded as measure-traps §44, with the rule: byte-level context search answers "how much of our byte
stream exists in the reference" and **must not** be read as "N% of this function is different code";
instruction-level comparison with address normalisation is the tool for "is this region displaced".

**Net effect on the row:** §109's original characterisation stands — the residue is displacement plus small
local differences — and round 1046's "four independent different-code regions" is withdrawn. All six
spellings targeting the first cluster's neighbourhood remain measured and losing (§24).

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1049 — verified codegen-walls §2's epilogue-merge claim byte-for-byte; the row's divergence is that wall

Round 1048's sound instrument put `gv_ExAllocGraveyardWorker` at an 84.8% prefix with its first
modulo-address difference at instruction 145, where the reference reads `pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp;
mov eax,0xffff` and ours reads `mov eax,0xffff; pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp`. That looks like a four-instruction
epilogue reorder.

**It is codegen-walls §2, verified exactly.** The 13-byte epilogue

```
5f 5e 5d b8 ff ff 00 00 5b 83 c4 10 c3
pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp; mov eax,0xffff; pop ebx; add esp,0x10; ret
```

occurs **twice** in the reference `.text` — at `0x10011cdb` and `0x10011d77` — and **once** in ours
(`0x10011cdb`). The reference keeps two copies and routes the entry-search loop's three exits to the later
one; we emit one and fold all three into it. My measured "reorder" is our single copy starting at the offset
where the reference's *second* copy starts.

**Three spellings measured at the link on this epilogue, all reverted:**

| spelling | link delta |
|---|---|
| `fail_ffff:` returns via an `unsigned short fail_val = 0xffff;` temp | **+0** (optimised away, order unchanged) |
| the direct `return 0xffff` at line 521 converted to `goto fail_ffff` | **+321** |
| (a `gv_fail_code()` call variant was drafted and **not** tested — it changes semantics and so cannot be byte-identical even if it scored well) | not run |

The +0 row is the informative one: giving the constant a named temp does not delay its materialisation, so
the epilogue's order is not a statement-order property. The +321 row reproduces §2's mechanism from the
source side — merging the two exits explicitly makes the object much worse.

**Also confirmed:** the carrier's own header mis-diagnoses this row as "an ecx<->edx role exchange … a
register-naming difference, not a shape difference". The registers are identical at every index; what differs
is which epilogue copy three branches reach. §2 already records that mis-diagnosis and the reason a
stream diff (and a positional ruler) cannot see it — the check that finds it is comparing **branch targets**.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change retained; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1050 — tested whether §2's epilogue-merge wall generalises; it does not, and the one row it touched is closed

Round 1049 confirmed codegen-walls §2 on `gv_ExAllocGraveyardWorker` (the reference keeps two copies of a
13-byte epilogue, we keep one). If that wall were general, it would explain residue on many carriers at once,
so it was worth testing across all 19.

**Method.** Count the characteristic epilogue signature `pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp` (`5f 5e 5d`) in the
reference against ours, per carrier.

**Result: it touches two rows, and one of them is a false positive.**

| carrier | reference | ours | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cm_ExCopyEntityData` | 1 | 0 | real, but **a different wall** — see below |
| `CrashDump` | 0 | 1 | **false positive**: the function tails are byte-identical; the count differs only because my window has different extents for the two images |

The other 17 carriers show equal counts. **§2's wall is per-site, not general** — consistent with its own
record that it merges only *byte-identical* exits, which is rare.

**`cm_ExCopyEntityData` was examined and is already closed.** Its reference has two `ret` sites
(`0x1000ed7c`, `0x1000edb4`) against our one, so it initially looked like a third §2 instance. Disassembling
`0x1000ed40..` shows the actual divergence is **the clamp**, not an epilogue:

```
ref  0x1000ed4d jle 0x1000ed56 ; cmp eax,0x7f ; jge 0x1000ed5d ; jmp 0x1000ed62
     0x1000ed56 mov eax,0xffffff81 ; jmp 0x1000ed62      <- low arm, inline
     0x1000ed5d mov eax,0x7f                            <- high arm, inline
     0x1000ed62 mov byte ptr [edx+ecx], al
our  0x1000ed4d jle 0x1000ed85 ; cmp eax,0x7f ; jl 0x1000ed59 ; mov eax,0x7f
     0x1000ed59 mov byte ptr [ecx+edx], al
```

We branch away to an out-of-line low clamp that is **9 bytes shorter**. This is documented in full at
**shapes §124** — including both arms, the shared store, the 9-byte shortfall, and the two spellings measured
at the link and rejected (**+3** for the reference's two-arm form, and **+76,125** for an arm swap that
changed semantics and spread damage across thirteen functions). Cross-checked: `scripts/whathas.py` lists
shapes §62, §63, §64, §85 and §124 for this row, and §63's own rule is "a clamp's winning arm order is
per-site, not per-function".

**No probe spent, and none warranted.** Recorded so the §2-generalisation hypothesis is not re-tried: it is
per-site, it touches two rows, and both are accounted for.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283 (264 byte-matched), residue 8628
(`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1052 — fixed the build-tree drift bug; added gate + linktest guards; restored the tree

**The incident.** Round 1051's toolchain sweep substituted `/REBREW_TOOLCHAIN:<name>` in
`build/CMakeFiles/server_dll.dir/build.make` to test nine msvc6 images. Restoring the file was **not
sufficient**: the objects had been recompiled under swept flags, and `build/split_poc` held a stale
composition. The tree was left measuring **58% residue** (`0x14063`) and a **290,816-byte** deliverable,
against the correct **8628** and **286,720**.

**Restored.** `rm -rf build`, then a clean
`cmake -B build -S . --toolchain cmake/toolchain-msvc-6.0-sp6-docker.cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
-DREBREW_DEBUG_INFO=OFF`, full build, `--target final`. Verified:

```
residue 8628, raw-link .data 21481, verify 281/283, byte-matched 264, imports 100
cmp .scratch/shipped.before.dll build/server.dll  ->  BIT-IDENTICAL
md5sum                                            ->  3febd2c4ca080a3749c12d4bf7452fbe (both)
```

**The bug fixed.** `build/` is gitignored, so a hand-edited `build.make` is invisible to `git status`,
lint, verify and `cmake --build` alike, while silently redefining what every `linktest.sh` measurement
means. New **`scripts/build_tree_check.py`** compares CMake's own per-object flag record (`flags.make`'s
`# Custom flags: <obj>_FLAGS = ...` comments) against the compile line `build.make` carries, and reports any
codegen flag token that is in one and not the other. Wired into **`gate.sh`** as `== build-tree integrity`
(fails the gate) and into **`linktest.sh`** (exit 4, refuses to measure).

**Verified both directions:**

| test | result |
|---|---|
| clean tree | `build.make agrees with flags.make (198 object(s) with recorded flags)`, exit 0 |
| one injected `/Ob1` in one object's rule | `DRIFT: 1 unrecorded flag token(s)`, gate fails, linktest exits 4 |

**A second bug, found while writing the checker.** `parse_recorded` compiled its pattern **without `re.M`**,
so `$` anchored to end-of-*string* and it matched **zero** of the 202 `Custom` comments — the checker
printed "agrees" while comparing nothing. A guard that silently checks nothing is worse than no guard. Fixed,
and the summary now prints the count it compared so a zero is visible.

**Not an upstream `rebrew` bug:** grepped the installed package — `rebrew` never reads `build.make`, so the
exposure is entirely in this project's scripts, and that is where the fix lives.

Recorded as workflow-traps §20. Committed: `scripts/build_tree_check.py`, `scripts/gate.sh`,
`scripts/linktest.sh`.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1053 — three real bugs fixed in tooling; tree composition failure diagnosed (pre-existing, unfixed)

Started from the user's instruction to fix every rebrew bug encountered and keep docs current. Three
genuine bugs found and fixed, and one **pre-existing, reproducible composition failure** characterised.

### Bug 1 — `map_libcmt.py` crashed on any VA absent from the catalog (FIXED)

```
File "scripts/map_libcmt.py", line 450, in <genexpr>
    ids = sorted(order[v] for v, _ in funcs)
KeyError: 268545824        # 0x1001af20
```

`order` is built from the catalog `rows`, while `funcs` are matched hits; a hit can sit at a VA the
catalog does not list (`0x1001af20` is not in `db/server.dll_functions.csv`). The lookup aborted the entire
report. Fixed to compute contiguity over the VAs that are present and **name** the absent ones, so a
catalog gap is visible rather than fatal.

### Bug 2 — `emit_defs.py` could exit its fixed-point loop silently (FIXED)

`for _round in range(6): ... if not missing: break` had no failure path: exhausting the cap left the link
with an incomplete definition set and the failure surfaced later as a composition collapse or phantom
residue, never as "did not converge". Added a `for...else` that raises with the count and the first few
missing symbols. Measured: the real tree converges in **2 passes** (73 -> 0), so the branch is unreachable
today — it exists so that if it is ever reached, it says so.

### Bug 3 — postlink's `.rdata` prefix error named one cause and hid the measurement (FIXED in the rebrew checkout)

The message said "check the debug directory: builds with /debug carry an extra 0x1c-byte directory". The
actual discrepancy here was **+64 bytes** with `DataDirectory[6] == 0` in **both** images — no debug

measured prefix length, the IAT and import-directory RVAs, and the reference's expected length, and to

different length. Recorded as workflow-traps §21.

`cmake --build build --target final` fails on a **completely clean** rebuild:


| section | reference | built | delta |
|---|---|---|---|

| `.rdata` | `0x2e81` | `0x2ec1` | **+64** |
| `.data` | `0x174059c` | `0x1740338` | −612 |
| `.reloc` | `0x10374` | `0x83dc` | −32664 |

**Ruled out as causes:**

## Round 1054 — faking the original `D:\` path is possible (verified) and currently unnecessary (measured)

Answering "can we fake the original folder structure through cmake/docker/wine?" — **yes, two lines, verified
by experiment**, and **it changes nothing today**.

**The technique.** The wineprefix is a host directory mounted into the container, and wine reads drives from
`{prefix}/dosdevices/`. A fresh prefix has only `c:` and `z:`; adding a `d:` symlink creates the drive:

```bash
mkdir -p .scratch/Ddrive/Develop/DieGildeAddOnServer
ln -s $PWD/.scratch/Ddrive ~/.cache/rebrew-msvc-6.0-sp6-wineprefix/dosdevices/d:
rebrew-cmake-cl /nologo /c /O2 /Gd /MT /Foout.obj "D:\\Develop\\DieGildeAddOnServer\\server.c"
strings out.obj | grep server.c
#   D:\Develop\DieGildeAddOnServer\server.c      <- byte-identical to the reference
```

**Constraint found by experiment:** the `d:` target must live inside a directory the container already
mounts. `_docker_run` mounts exactly two — the project root and the wineprefix — so a `d:` pointing at
`/tmp` fails with `C1083` even though the symlink itself is correct. Verified both ways.

**The measurement that makes it unnecessary.** `__FILE__` appears **nowhere** in the tree (`grep -rn
"__FILE__" src/server.dll` finds one hit, in a comment). Every `D:\Develop\...` string is a **hand-written
literal**:

```c
LogMessageInternal("D:\\Develop\\DieGildeAddOnServer\\server.c", 0x5df, "LOBBY mode", 1);
```

- **14** `D:\Develop\...`-shaped strings exist in the reference, and **all 14 are already present in the
  shipped file** (scanned both images).
- **11** distinct literals are written out in the sources.

So the path axis is closed by construction. The original almost certainly used literals too — had it used
`__FILE__`, the strings would carry MSVC's own `D:\`-relative layout and `/FC` would have been needed.

**When it would matter:** if a round ever converts one of these literals to `__FILE__` (while tidying, or
because a decompiler emitted `__FILE__` for a path argument), the build would silently emit `Z:\home\maci\...`
and break `.rdata` strings that match today. The `d:` mapping above is the fix at that point.

Recorded in `general-knowledge.md` with the mechanism, the mount constraint, and the reason it is unused.
Experiments cleaned up (`dosdevices/d:` removed, scratch dirs deleted).

**State:** `build/server.dll` is the restored known-good file; the gate fails on the **pre-existing
composition bug** characterised in round 1053 (`.text` +1264, `.rdata` +64 on a fresh composition), which
remains the open item.

## Round 1057 — fixed a silent-pass defect in the build-check I just added

Applied last round's lesson (test your own tooling as hard as the target) to `rebrew build-check`, and found
a defect in the direction that matters: **a mistyped `--build-dir` exited 0.**

```
$ rebrew build-check --build-dir /nonexistent
build-check: /nonexistent is not configured -- nothing to check
$ echo $?
0
```

That is the *same failure shape the command exists to catch*: an unverifiable state reported as success.
Worse, it was reachable from the gate, which calls it as `if ! bc=$(rebrew build-check 2>&1)` — an
unconfigured tree would have passed the integrity check silently.

**Fixed:**

- `check()` now reports **which** file is missing (`build.make` vs `flags.make`) rather than saying the
  directory is "not configured", so a typo is diagnosable.
- `main()` exits non-zero unless the status is `ok` — drift **and** not-configured both fail.
- Five new tests, including `test_cli_exits_nonzero_when_not_configured`,
  `test_cli_exits_zero_on_a_clean_tree`, and `test_cli_exits_nonzero_on_drift`, which invoke the real Typer
  app through `CliRunner` and assert on `exit_code`.

**Verified through the installed CLI after reinstall:**

| invocation | output | exit |
|---|---|---|
| from `/tmp` (no project) | `... build.make does not exist -- build is not configured` | **1** |
| from the project, clean tree | `build.make agrees with flags.make (198 object(s) checked)` | **0** |

**Rebrew suite: 7167 passed**, one pre-existing failure (missing Dockerfiles for three unrelated
toolchains — confirmed by stashing). All pre-commit hooks pass.

**This is the third defect found in my own build-check work** (after the missing `re.M` flag that made it
compare zero objects, and the `emit_defs` mid-body insertion that broke the composition). The pattern in all
three: **a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a check that passes**, and I introduced it while
building something whose entire purpose was to close that gap. The tests now pin the exit codes, which is
what makes the regression detectable.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1058 — audited the remaining helper scripts for silent passes; corrected one stale docstring

Applied the last three rounds' lesson (test the tooling, not just the target) to the project's other
measurement scripts.

**Exit codes, run from the repo root:**

| script | exit | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_objective.py` | 0 | correct — independent PE verification passes |
| `object_span_check.py` | 1 | **correct** — one object is genuinely over its span (below) |
| `data_extent_check.py` | 1 | needs the venv (`ModuleNotFoundError: rebrew`) — invocation, not a defect |
| `section_geometry.py` | 1 | correct — `.reloc` raw `-0x9000` vs reference, which postlink replaces |

**`object_span_check.py` found a real, explainable datum.** Its docstring claimed the object measurement
treats **"zero are over"**; the tree now reports **1**:

```
OVER their span (1):
  mlock.c.obj      span 118   text 212   +94
```

**Investigated and it is not a defect.** `mlock.c` is a local LIBCMT replacement — the `_CRT_REGION_KEEP`
pattern, existing so the linker never pulls LIBCMT's `mlock.obj` (which imports
`FatalAppExitA`/`IsBadWritePtr`). Its object therefore carries CRT support code the two annotated functions
(`_mlock` at `0x1001d036`, `_munlock` at `0x1001d097`) do not describe. The extra 43-byte section sits at
`0x1001d0ac` and is **byte-correct in the deliverable** (0 differing bytes measured), so the overshoot does
not move later symbols.

**Docstring corrected** to record the measured state and to tell a reader that `over > 0` on a *replacement*
object means "this file also carries displaced library code", not "this file is broken". Checking the bytes
before acting is the discriminator.

**Also confirmed:** the "objects whose .text exceeds their annotated size" sweep is **empty** for every other
`.c.obj` in the build — `mlock.c` is the only such file, and for the reason above. So there is no
unannotated-code gap anywhere in the tree.

## Round 1059 — re-profiled the two spiel622.c carriers with the sound instrument; both confirm documented walls

Applied round 1048's corrected instrument (direct prefix walk + resync scan; **not** `SequenceMatcher`,
which measure-traps §45 shows reports 100% on streams that diverge at instruction 21) to the two carriers
that share `spiel622.c`, and decoded the exact divergence in each:

**`gm_CalculateProductionValue` (`0x10019720`, 5 residue)** — 127 instructions both sides, first difference at
index 68 (54% prefix), tail resync 5/58 at offset +1:

```
ref  fxch st(1)                    our  cmp byte ptr [esi], 0x17
ref  cmp byte ptr [esi], 0x17      our  fxch st(1)
```

An **adjacent pair swap**, exactly as `msvc6-c-shapes.md` §46 records: the `fxch` slot and the compare fold
are set by **one type choice** — a `float` local folds the compare but schedules it ahead of the `fxch`; a
`double` local gets the order right but loses the fold and emits `mov al,[esi]` + a later `cmp al,0x17`, one
byte longer. **The two cannot be steered apart.** The file header documents both spellings and their scores
across ~200 lines (lines 83-277). Measured now, reverted never — nothing was probed.

**`gm_CheckInventoryCapacity` (`0x10019ed0`, 97 residue)** — 138 vs 137 instructions, first difference at
index 8 (6% prefix), tail resync **107/128 at offset +1**:

```
ref  xor ebp, ebp                  our  mov dword ptr [esp+0x18], 0x12
```

The `in_list = 0` placement documented at round 1034, whose crux probe (hoisting `in_list` and `cap` with
`list[7] = in_list`) measured **+0** with the carrier unchanged.

**Neither row moved and neither has an unprobed lever.** Both are documented from multiple angles, and both
are among the 18 carriers whose walls this project has characterised.

**Also verified this round — the objective's load criterion at the byte level.** The built DLL's two exports,
located through the reference's own export directory:

| export | VA | 64-byte body |
|---|---|---|
| `Init` | `0x10009320` | **0 differing bytes** |
| `Exit` | `0x10009350` | **0 differing bytes** |

So the functions the DLL actually exposes are byte-identical, not merely loadable — which is the strongest
form of the "Wine load + exports resolve" criterion.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1060 — a read-only metadata file does not stop rebrew; /O1 closed on gm_AllocGebaeude

**Set out to sweep `/O1` across the nine carriers using default flags** — a bounded, real experiment on the
compiler-flag axis, which no round has run per-carrier. Two things came out of it, neither being the sweep.

**1. The build-check guard works and blocked the sweep.** Editing `build.make` to switch flags now exits 4
from `scripts/linktest.sh` with the restore command — the guard added in round 1052 doing exactly its job.
That also means `build.make` editing is no longer an available experiment path, which is the intended
trade. Restored from backup; `rebrew build-check` clean (198 objects).

**2. RETRACTED (round 1061): the read-only metadata is the DESIGNED write-lock, not a bug.** `src/rebrew-functions.toml` is
`-r--r--r--`, which stops a shell redirect or an editor — but not `rebrew`:

```
rebrew test <file> --cflags "/O1 /Gd"   ->  persisted `cflags = "/O1 /Gd"` into the metadata
```

Mechanism, **verified directly rather than inferred**: `rebrew.utils.atomic_write_text` writes a sibling temp
file and `os.replace()`s it onto the target. `os.replace` needs *directory* write permission, not file write
permission:

```
$ chmod 444 .scratch/rotest
$ python3 -c "import os,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('.scratch/rotest'); t=p.with_name('rotest.tmp'); \
              t.write_text('replaced'); os.replace(t,p)"
os.replace SUCCEEDED on a 444 file -> replaced
-rw-r--r-- 1 maci maci 8 ... rotest        <- and the read-only mode is gone
```

So a read-only metadata file is not a safety boundary. `chmod u+w` was needed to undo it. Reverted: pin
removed, mode restored, `git diff` on the file empty. Recorded as workflow-traps §23, with the safe
measurement procedure (snapshot and diff around every `rebrew test --cflags`).

**What the sweep measured before it had to stop.** `/O1 /Gd` on `gm_AllocGebaeude`, against the current
`/O2 /Gd`:

| flag set | status | match | obj |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/O2 /Gd` (current) | NEAR_MATCHING | **753** | 1078 |
| `/O1 /Gd` | SIZE_MISMATCH | **54** | 953 |

Catastrophically worse — 8.4% of the match count. That closes the `/O1` lead on this carrier without needing
the other eight; `/O1` is the flag 64 functions in this tree carry, so it was the plausible alternative, and
it is not one here.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

**CORRECTION (round 1061).** The read-only mode is **rebrew's write-lock discipline**, not a bug:
`rebrew.utils.atomic_write_locked` chmods the file writable, writes atomically, and re-locks to `0444` so
*hand* edits fail while the CLI is the sanctioned path. The explicit chmod-before is also required on
Windows, where `os.replace` over a read-only target fails, so it is load-bearing for atomicity rather than
policy. **Nothing to fix.**

Verified end to end: a `rebrew test` write updates the mtime (16:42 -> 16:44), restores mode `0444`, and
leaves the content hash unchanged (`bc846afe7505e0b92707aff505ac9520`) for a no-op update — the unlock/write/
re-lock cycle working exactly as documented. `workflow-traps.md` §23 is rewritten in place.

What **survives** from round 1060 and is the actually useful part: `rebrew test --cflags` **persists** a
per-function flag pin as a side effect of measuring, and that pin silently changes the flags the whole tree
resolves for that function — so every later `linktest.sh`/`gate.sh` measurement inherits it. Snapshot
`src/rebrew-functions.toml` before any `--cflags` probe and diff afterwards (workflow-traps §15). The file
mode is not what protects you here; the discipline is.

## Round 1063 — falsified the last predictor hypothesis: residue does not track x87, call, or branch density

Every prior round characterised carriers **individually**. This tested whether any **structural property
predicts residue size across the set** — the cheapest possible lead if it existed, and never tabulated.

| property | test | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| x87 instruction count | 2 x87-heavy carriers sit at **opposite extremes**: `gm_AllocSpieler` (128 ops) 2.67 residue/insn, `gm_CalculateProductionValue` (29 ops) **0.04**, the lowest in the set. Mean density x87-bearing **0.97** vs other fifteen **1.16** | **no correlation** |
| call count | highest-density carrier has **2 calls**; the two highest call counts (55) sit at 2.67 and **0.57**; `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity` has **zero calls** at 1.73 | **no correlation** |
| branch density | highest `jcc` count (96, `gm_AllocSpieler`) is high-density; second (88, `ServerMainThread`) is 0.57 — opposite ends | **no correlation** |

**What this rules out:** any explanation that is a function of instruction *mix*. Together with §23 (carriers
fail individually; 130/137 file-mates byte-identical), the residue is not predictable from gross structure. It
is a property of **specific scheduling and allocation decisions** in each function — which is exactly what the
per-carrier sections describe, and why no shortcut to them exists.

**Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §27** with the full 19-row table. Six consecutive rounds re-confirmed
individual walls; this is the first that tested the *set* and came back negative. That is worth having
precisely because a positive correlation would have been the cheapest possible lead.

**No source, metadata or `build.make` change; nothing to revert.**

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1064 — `#pragma function(memset)` on the largest carrier: cannot be measured (composition breaks)

`gm_AllocSpieler` (2,823 of 8,628 residue bytes) declares `#pragma intrinsic(memcpy, memset, strlen, strcpy)`,
and its header plus shapes §109 both reason about "the memset call". No round had tried the opposite —
forcing a real out-of-line call with `#pragma function(memset)`. Tried it.

**Result: the experiment cannot produce a number.** `linktest.sh` reports the round-232 guard:

```
COMPOSITION COLLAPSED: only 0 symbols landed at their reference VA.
```

The out-of-line `memset` reference breaks the per-reference-offset composition before any residue
measurement exists. That is a stronger statement than "it measured worse" — the spelling is not merely
inferior, it is incompatible with the link this tree requires.

**The aftermath is the more useful finding.** Reverting the source was **not enough**: with the file restored
and `git diff` clean, the composition still collapsed across a fresh `rm -rf build/split_poc &&
split_link.sh`, repeatedly. Cause: the **stale object** still held the version compiled under the other
pragma, and `split_link.sh` links objects, not source. **Recovery required a full `cmake --build build`**,
after which `exactly at their reference VA: 246` and residue **8628** returned.

**`linktest.sh`'s stale-object guard does not catch this.** It warns when the *source is newer* than the
object. After a revert the timestamps end up consistent, so no warning fires while the object holds the
experiment's code. Recorded as workflow-traps §24 with the rule: after any pragma / intrinsic / codegen-flag
change, treat the object as poisoned — revert the source **and** run `cmake --build build` before measuring.
A collapse that survives a clean `split_link.sh` is the tell.

**Cost:** three recovery cycles in this round, all self-inflicted by measuring before rebuilding.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK. Source tree
clean (`git status -- src/` empty).

## Round 1065 — linktest's collapse message now names both fixes, not just the one that does not work

Round 1064 cost three recovery cycles because `linktest.sh`'s composition-collapse message gave only the
round-232 fix:

```
Fix with:  rm -rf build/split_poc && bash scripts/split_link.sh
```

That is correct for a stale *workspace* and **insufficient** for a stale *object* — the pragma case, where
the collapse survives it and only a full `cmake --build build` recovers. The message sent me to the fix that
does not work, three times.

**Now it escalates:**

```
COMPOSITION COLLAPSED: only N symbols landed at their reference VA.
         Every residue number below would be meaningless.
         Try, in this order:
             1) rm -rf build/split_poc && bash scripts/split_link.sh
                (if that restores the placement, the workspace was stale)
             2) cmake --build build   # recompile EVERY object
                Needed when the collapse survives step 1: a source experiment
                that changed a pragma/intrinsic/codegen flag leaves the OBJECT
                holding the experimental code, and no mtime check catches it.
```

**Verified:** simulated a collapse in `.scratch/linktest-link.log` (rewrote `246` to `0`); the guard parses
`placed=0` and fires with the new text. Restored the log; `linktest.sh` clean at **+0** and the gate passes.

**Why the message is the right place rather than a new check.** Checked directly whether a stale object can
be detected: it **cannot**. A pragma leaves **no trace** in the `.obj` to grep for (`strings` on
`gm_AllocSpieler.c.obj` finds no pragma/intrinsic/memset reference), and the existing mtime comparison passes
once `git checkout` rewrites the source and a build updates the object. So the collapse *is* the signal, and
the only improvement available is to make the message name both fixes — which it now does.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1066 — located the `strcpy`-inlining divergence on m_AllocTracked; it has two independent causes

Surveyed pragma usage after round 1064 (`m_AllocTracked.c` carries **10 pragmas**, the most in the tree). Its
header documents the `memset` half exhaustively and mentions `0x100066a0-0x100066b7` only as the reason
`#pragma function(memset, strcpy)` was rejected. **Decoding that address in the shipped form shows a live
divergence the record does not describe** — the reference and our build emit msvc6's inlined `strcpy`
differently:

```
reference                     ours
0x100066a0 cld                0x100066a0 not  ecx
0x100066a1 repne scasb        0x100066a2 sub  edi, ecx
0x100066a3 not   ecx          0x100066a4 mov  eax, ecx
0x100066a5 sub   edi, ecx     0x100066a6 shr  ecx, 2      <- ours schedules it here
0x100066a9 mov   esi, edi     0x100066a9 mov  esi, edi
0x100066ab mov   edi, edx     0x100066ab mov  edi, edx
0x100066ad shr   ecx, 2       0x100066ad rep  movsd
0x100066b0 rep   movsd        ...                          <- reference schedules it here
```

**Two independent differences:** the reference has **`cld; repne scasb`** (4 bytes) at the head where ours has
nothing, **and** `shr ecx,2` is scheduled two instructions apart.

**Quantified:** 21 of the 25 bytes at that site differ. The carrier's **92 residue bytes form 12 clusters**
(`+0x11`, `+0x2e`, `+0xfa`, `+0x113..0x128`, `+0x12d..0x141`, `+0x147..0x14d`, `+0x179`, `+0x19f`, `+0x1d5`,
`+0x1fb`, `+0x22d`, `+0x252..0x265`), so this is one cluster of twelve, not the whole row.

**Recorded, not probed — and the reasoning matters.** `cld` before `repne scasb` is **optional** (the ABI
guarantees DF=0 on entry), so its presence is a codegen choice rather than a semantic need; the `shr ecx,2`
position is a scheduler decision. Both are the class this project has measured repeatedly as unreachable from
C on this compiler. The header already establishes the two pragma splits are mutually exclusive and states the
target's combination *"was not built with the msvc6 SP6 codegen this project has"* — this divergence is
**independent supporting evidence** for that claim: the reference's `strcpy` expansion carries a `cld`
preamble our compiler does not emit there.

Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §28. What is new is that the `strcpy` half is now precisely located and
characterised rather than cited as a rejection reason.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1067 — positive evidence for the asm clause: the reference's `strcpy` carries a `cld` msvc6 never emits

Round 1066 located `m_AllocTracked`'s `strcpy`-inlining divergence at `0x100066a0`. This round probed its
**first cause**: the reference begins `cld; repne scasb`; ours begins at `repne scasb`.

**Tested whether any C spelling produces the `cld`** — three independent compiles under this file's own flags,
each isolating the expansion:

| spelling | emitted head |
|---|---|
| `strcpy(dst, src)` with `<string.h>` | `83 c9 ff 33 c0 f2 ae f7 d1 2b f9 8b c1 8b f7 ...` |
| same + `#pragma intrinsic(strcpy)` | identical |
| same, `dst`/`src` as parameters | identical shape |

**None emits `cld`.** All three go `33 c0` → `f2 ae`. The reference is `fc f2 ae f7 d1 2b f9 8b c1 ...` —
**`cld` followed by byte-for-byte what all three spellings produce** (`ref_head == b'\xfc' + our_head` is
`True`). The in-situ build agrees: our compiled `m_AllocTracked` has the expansion starting
`8d 7d e8 f2 ae f7 d1 ...`, no `cld` adjacent.

**Why this is real evidence rather than a quirk.** The x86 ABI guarantees DF=0 on entry, so a compiler
emitting `repne scasb` — including an *inlined* `strcpy` — has no need to clear it. msvc6's expansion does not
emit `cld` in any of three forms tested. The reference emits it anyway. That is precisely the objective's
allowed justification: *"a code shape no MSVC6 C output can produce"*.

**A caveat found while testing, recorded because it nearly misled the round.** The isolated compiles schedule
`shr ecx,2` **after** `mov esi,edi`; the in-situ build places it **before**. So the expansion's schedule is
**context-dependent**, and isolated probes answer the `cld` question (all three agree on its absence) but must
not be used to reason about `shr` ordering, which §28 measured in situ.

**Why it is still not a lever.** One byte, on a carrier whose 92 residue bytes span **12 clusters**; the
surrounding schedule difference is a separate context-dependent cause that no pragma reaches. Closing it
would need `__asm { cld }` at that site and would still leave eleven clusters. **Recorded as evidence, not as
a probe target** — a distinction the objective makes explicitly, and the first time this project has had
positive grounds for it on a residual site.

Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §29.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.

## Round 1068 — the `cld` is one site in eighteen; scale measured, and my own summary corrected

Round 1067 established that the reference's inlined `strcpy` at `m_AllocTracked` carries a `cld` our msvc6
never emits. This round measured whether that is a compiler habit or a one-off.

**Scanned the whole reference `.text` for `f2 ae` (`repne scasb`): 18 sites. Exactly ONE is preceded by `cld`
(`0x100066a0`). Our build emits `cld; repne scasb` zero times.**

The 15 other sites share the same `83 c9 ff 33 c0` prologue idiom; the `cld` site is the only one whose
preceding byte is `55` (an unrelated `push ebp`). So the `cld` is **not** a systematic codegen variant — it is
one site, which strengthens §29's reading: no C spelling produces it, and the reference has it once.

**A correction to my own round-1067 closing summary.** I wrote "the 17 normal sites are byte-correct in our
build; only the `cld` site is not." **Wrong: 6 of the 17 differ.** Those six sit inside residue carriers, so
their difference is expected displacement rather than a `cld` matter — but the sentence overstated the
evidence as measured, and it is corrected in place in `codegen-walls.md` §30 rather than dropped.

**The arithmetic, now explicit.** One byte, at one of eighteen `repne scasb` sites, on a carrier whose 92
residue bytes span **12 clusters** — eleven of which have nothing to do with this. `cld` remains genuine
positive evidence for the objective's asm clause (no C spelling emitted it), and it is decisively **not** a
lever.

Recorded as `codegen-walls.md` §30.

**State:** gate pass — build-tree integrity OK, lint 188/188, compile 0 errors, verify 281/283
(264 byte-matched), residue 8628 (`0x21b4`), raw-link `.data` 21481, imports 100, wine load OK.
